title: Scope-preserving direct object access
invariant: Every direct read or mutation preserves the caller's tenant, ownership, relationship, visibility, and action scope through the final object operation.
attackerControl: The caller selects an object identifier or invokes a direct get, update, delete, follow, abort, download, or similar fast path.
differential: List or canonical read paths apply an authorization predicate, while the direct path resolves or mutates by identifier alone or loses a scope dimension before the store.
requiredProof: Trace the direct path to the protected store, show the exact omitted predicate, establish how the caller obtains or guesses the identifier, and demonstrate an out-of-scope read or state change.
decisiveRejection: A scoped repository, row-level policy, atomic conditional mutation, or post-resolution check enforces the complete caller tuple for the exact object and action.
overlaps: ACX-07, ACX-14, ACX-24, PTX-09

title: Equivalent mutation policy parity
invariant: Every path capable of producing the same protected state enforces the same field, role, transition, and action policy.
attackerControl: The caller chooses an alternate verb, content type, import, overwrite, restore, clone, compatibility route, or update representation.
differential: A canonical mutation protects sensitive fields or transitions, while an equivalent path reaches the same state through different validation or authorization logic.
requiredProof: Show that the weaker path is independently reachable by the attacker and can produce a state the secure sibling denies, including normalization and downstream model behavior.
decisiveRejection: All representations converge on one normalized command and the same authoritative field and transition policy before persistence.
overlaps: ACX-19, ACX-20, PDX-05, RIX-07

title: Caller scope after privilege elevation
invariant: Switching to an internal, system, or otherwise elevated client must preserve and reapply the initiating caller's permitted resource, tenant, action, and field scope.
attackerControl: The caller reaches a code path that uses elevated storage, network, orchestration, or service credentials after initial authentication.
differential: The outer layer checks only coarse route access, then the elevated layer resolves or changes a broader resource set without reconstructing the caller predicate.
requiredProof: Identify the exact elevated identity, the caller predicate lost at the boundary, and a resource or effect reachable by the elevated client but forbidden to the initiating caller.
decisiveRejection: The elevated operation receives an integrity-protected caller context and enforces the complete caller tuple at or immediately before the sink.
overlaps: ACX-04, ACX-05, ACX-06, QEX-02

title: Privilege and resource scope alignment
invariant: The scope of an independently grantable privilege must be at least as broad as every resource, storage namespace, and fan-out target it controls.
attackerControl: A caller with local or tenant-scoped authority invokes an operation backed by shared or deployment-wide storage, deterministic keys, wildcard selection, or global artifacts.
differential: The guard authorizes a narrow logical resource while the sink addresses or modifies a broader physical or derived resource.
requiredProof: Resolve every downstream key and target, demonstrate that the affected scope exceeds the grant, and show that no separate broader privilege is required.
decisiveRejection: Storage keys and fan-out targets are isolated by the full authority tuple, or a distinct correctly scoped privilege authorizes the broader operation.
overlaps: ACX-07, ACX-15, CBX-01, QEX-08

title: Delegated authority confinement
invariant: Lower-authority users cannot cause their content or parameters to execute with a more powerful user's, connector's, service account's, or worker's unrestricted authority.
attackerControl: The attacker creates or edits stored executable content, task parameters, integration configuration, workflow steps, or other input consumed later.
differential: Content is authorized under the author but later executed using another principal without immutable approval, least-privilege intersection, or sink-time authorization.
requiredProof: Record `A`, `T`, and `E`, identify the exact credential at the sink, demonstrate `E`'s authority exceeds `A`'s, and show attacker-controlled behavior reaches a forbidden effect.
decisiveRejection: Execution uses an author-bound scoped capability, an intentional least-privilege intersection, or reauthorizes every resolved action and target against the appropriate current principal.
overlaps: ACX-12, ACX-18, ACX-30, QEX-02

title: Fail-closed execution provenance
invariant: Security behavior must be selected by authentic, integrity-protected execution provenance, with missing and unknown provenance receiving the most restrictive policy.
attackerControl: A caller omits, forges, replays, or reaches a path that fails to propagate a source, caller type, security context, or execution-mode marker.
differential: Direct requests set a restrictive context, while worker, workflow, plugin, internal, or AI paths default to broader behavior when the context is absent or untrusted.
requiredProof: Trace the provenance value to the policy branch, show how the weaker value is selected, and demonstrate a protected operation or output that becomes reachable.
decisiveRejection: Provenance is derived from an unforgeable runtime boundary, propagated end to end, and missing or unknown values fail closed.
overlaps: ACX-03, ACX-08, ACX-27, QEX-01

title: Authorization tuple preservation in queries and caches
invariant: Queries, search strategies, memoization, and cache keys preserve every security-relevant dimension and cannot reuse a broader result for a narrower caller.
attackerControl: The caller selects identifiers, query modes, strategy flags, cacheable inputs, tenant values, or request ordering that influences lookup and reuse.
differential: A scoped query or cache population path includes caller context, while a fast path, alternate strategy, key, or final query omits or canonicalizes it differently.
requiredProof: Show a concrete key collision, strategy switch, or final query that returns or changes a resource outside the caller's authority.
decisiveRejection: Both keys and final data queries include the complete normalized authority tuple, and results are revalidated on consumption and invalidated on authority changes.
overlaps: ACX-01, ACX-04, ACX-16, CBX-01, CBX-05

title: Authentic AI and tool state transitions
invariant: Trusted conversation roles, approvals, tool results, and function transitions are server-created and cannot substitute for independent authorization of a tool and its target.
attackerControl: The client supplies or modifies role labels, tool calls, function results, approval state, run identifiers, or conversation history.
differential: The guard trusts client-described AI state, while the runtime treats that state as authority to select or invoke a privileged tool.
requiredProof: Demonstrate acceptance of a forged transition and trace it to a tool effect the caller cannot invoke directly.
decisiveRejection: Trusted state is integrity-bound to an authentic server run and each resolved tool, action, resource, and credential is reauthorized independently.
overlaps: ACX-06, ACX-11, ACX-18, AIX-02

title: Complete capability binding
invariant: A token, signed URL, delegated credential, or other capability is bound to the complete canonical operation it authorizes.
attackerControl: The attacker obtains a valid capability and varies method, action, audience, tenant, resource, representation, version, constraints, or time of use.
differential: Verification authenticates a partial tuple, while the sink consumes additional attacker-selected dimensions not covered by the signature or scope.
requiredProof: Show that one valid capability can be replayed or repurposed for a distinct forbidden operation and identify the omitted binding.
decisiveRejection: Verification reconstructs and compares the same canonical tuple consumed by the sink, including freshness and single-use semantics where required.
overlaps: ACX-11, ACX-26, ACX-30, RIX-03

title: Approval bound to immutable semantics
invariant: Approval authorizes immutable content and context, not only a mutable identifier or container.
attackerControl: A lower-authority actor can edit, replace, retarget, delete and recreate, or relink content after approval but before execution.
differential: The approval guard records an identifier or stale snapshot, while execution resolves the latest script, destination, policy, workflow, connector, or other semantics.
requiredProof: Demonstrate post-approval mutation and later resolution of the changed content, and identify the forbidden effect that retains approval.
decisiveRejection: Approval binds the immutable digest or version, type, tenant, action, destination, and relevant constraints, or every dependent approval is invalidated atomically.
overlaps: ACX-13, ACX-29, ACX-32, SMX-06

title: Resolved discriminator authority
invariant: Schema selection, availability, and authorization derive from the authoritative resolved instance and agree on its type, subtype, action, and capability.
attackerControl: The caller supplies both an identifier and a declared type, kind, action, handler, tool, connector, or subtype.
differential: Validation or authorization trusts the declared discriminator, while runtime dispatch resolves the identifier to a different, more privileged instance.
requiredProof: Show a mismatch between declared and authoritative discriminator and trace the resolved instance to a forbidden sink.
decisiveRejection: One authoritative resolution supplies type, schema, policy, and dispatch, with explicit equality checks for any caller-supplied discriminator.
overlaps: ACX-08, ACX-09, PDX-05, QEX-04

title: Event subscriber principal confinement
invariant: Event-driven content executes with authority intentionally granted to the subscriber, not the unrestricted authority of an event producer or dispatcher.
attackerControl: A lower-authority actor registers or edits a listener, rule, subscription, callback, workflow, or event-triggered action.
differential: Subscription creation checks the author, but event dispatch supplies the producer's or system's stronger credential to attacker-controlled behavior.
requiredProof: Record `A`, `T`, and `E`, show that `A` controls the executed behavior, prove `E` exceeds `A`, and demonstrate a forbidden target or action.
decisiveRejection: The subscriber stores an author-scoped capability, execution uses a deliberate least-privilege intersection, or each effect is authorized against the subscriber's current authority.
overlaps: ACX-05, ACX-06, QEX-02, QEX-08

title: Side-effect authorization during replay and simulation
invariant: Replay, retry, backfill, resume, simulation, and lifecycle-control operations cannot retain side effects the current caller is not authorized to execute.
attackerControl: The caller selects stored work, replay mode, retry options, transformation flags, or defaults that preserve actions and destinations.
differential: The route authorizes only lifecycle control or observation, while transformed stored work still dispatches previously configured effects.
requiredProof: Identify a retained effect, show the caller lacks current permission for it, and trace it through transformation and dispatch to the real sink.
decisiveRejection: Side effects default off for non-execution modes or every retained action and target is reauthorized against the current appropriate principal.
overlaps: ACX-10, ACX-26, QEX-05, QEX-06

title: Complete selected-target authorization
invariant: Authorization covers the exact final resource selected by every identifier, revision, alias, child, attachment, relationship, or secondary selector.
attackerControl: The caller supplies a base object plus a selector that changes the effective resource or representation used at the sink.
differential: The guard checks an envelope, parent, base version, or route identifier, while the sink resolves a different child, revision, alias target, or related object.
requiredProof: Compare canonical guard and sink tuples and demonstrate that the final selected target is outside the caller's authority.
decisiveRejection: Resolution precedes authorization and the policy checks the canonical final type, identifier, tenant, relationship, representation, and action.
overlaps: ACX-01, ACX-11, ACX-28, PTX-09

title: Effective collection authorization
invariant: Authorization applies to the complete effective set after defaults, expansion, deduplication, wildcards, and special empty or omitted semantics.
attackerControl: The caller supplies omitted, empty, wildcard, duplicate, mixed-validity, multi-scope, nested, or very large selectors.
differential: The guard checks the submitted set, a representative element, or a vacuously true predicate, while the sink expands or interprets a broader set.
requiredProof: Derive both submitted and effective sets and show at least one resolved member or scope outside the caller's intended union or intersection of authority.
decisiveRejection: The effective set is resolved first, every member is intersected with caller scope, empty semantics fail closed, and the authorized set alone reaches the sink.
overlaps: ACX-04, ACX-20, QEX-08, REX-02

title: Structural authorization predicates
invariant: Mandatory owner, tenant, visibility, and policy predicates remain structural and cannot be altered by attacker-controlled query grammar.
attackerControl: The attacker influences a username, tenant, field, value, fragment, quote, wildcard, Boolean operator, serialized filter, or other query component.
differential: The guard intends to append a mandatory scope predicate, while textual composition, precedence, parsing, or normalization lets attacker input regroup or neutralize it.
requiredProof: Trace the constructed query or policy expression to its parser and demonstrate that the effective predicate returns or changes protected data outside scope.
decisiveRejection: Values are bound parameters or typed syntax nodes, field and operator choices are allowlisted, and inspection of the final parsed form confirms the security predicate remains mandatory.
overlaps: ACX-07, PDX-01, QIX-01

title: Privilege matched to output and effect
invariant: An independently grantable privilege authorizes every actual response field and side effect, regardless of route name, permission label, or nominal operation.
attackerControl: The caller invokes a route described as read, view, test, validate, manage, preview, or another apparently limited action and selects inputs affecting its behavior.
differential: The guard checks a weaker named privilege, while the implementation returns protected material or aborts, schedules, dispatches, rotates, deletes, executes, or otherwise performs a stronger effect.
requiredProof: Trace the independently grantable privilege to the concrete output and sinks, and show the attacker's role is denied the equivalent canonical read or action.
decisiveRejection: The checked privilege explicitly covers the actual fields and effects, or separate authoritative checks protect each stronger operation before it occurs.
overlaps: ACX-21, SDX-01, SDX-07

title: Bounded privilege over bounded primitives
invariant: A privilege for saved, approved, templated, or otherwise constrained operations cannot reach an arbitrary query, command, script, target, override, or execution primitive.
attackerControl: The caller supplies raw statements, free-form code, targets, variable overrides, environment values, or parameters beyond the intended template.
differential: The guard authorizes a semantically bounded operation, while the sink accepts a more expressive attacker-controlled primitive.
requiredProof: Demonstrate that input escapes the approved semantic subset and performs a forbidden operation or reaches a forbidden target under the weaker privilege.
decisiveRejection: Immutable approved content, strict typed schemas, allowlisted targets, constrained capabilities, and sink authorization preserve the intended subset end to end.
overlaps: ACX-05, ACX-08, CIX-04, QIX-06

title: Domain policy through generic facades
invariant: Generic CRUD, proxy, wrapper, connector, exception, compatibility, and convenience interfaces preserve the protected subtype's authoritative domain policy.
attackerControl: The caller chooses a protected subtype, operation, protocol, media type, generic endpoint, or alternate interface.
differential: The canonical domain path applies type-specific authorization, while the generic facade resolves the same object or effect using only coarse or unrelated checks.
requiredProof: Compare both paths to the same sink and show which caller, type, action, scope, field, or lifecycle predicate the facade loses.
decisiveRejection: The facade dispatches to the same authoritative policy after resolving the final domain object and operation.
overlaps: ACX-02, ACX-11, ACX-17, RIX-07

title: Per-item and per-field batch authorization
invariant: Every effective item, nested object, protected field, and partial write in a batch is authorized before unauthorized state can persist.
attackerControl: The caller mixes authorized and unauthorized records, tenants, namespaces, fields, operations, or ordering within one bulk request.
differential: The guard checks the envelope, first element, one namespace, or representative item, while the sink processes other members or commits incrementally.
requiredProof: Construct a mixed-authority batch, trace validation and failure order, and show an unauthorized item or field is returned or persisted.
decisiveRejection: The system resolves and authorizes every effective member and field before an atomic commit, or failures provably cannot retain unauthorized results.
overlaps: ACX-02, ACX-15, SMX-04

title: Secret-read privilege lattice separation
invariant: Independently grantable secret use, test, write, rotate, import, reference, and administrative privileges must not authorize the plaintext-read or decrypt-and-return action.
attackerControl: The caller holds a non-read capability and selects a route, operation, action name, privilege combination, generic facade, or role composition that can invoke secret retrieval.
differential: The authoritative privilege mapping or route gate treats a weaker non-read capability as sufficient for an operation whose semantic result is plaintext secret access.
requiredProof: Demonstrate that the non-read privilege is independently grantable, trace the exact authorization decision to the plaintext-read operation, and show the caller gains a value denied by the canonical explicit read privilege.
decisiveRejection: The privilege lattice requires a distinct narrowly scoped secret-read capability at the authoritative retrieval or decrypt-and-return operation, independent of response-channel hardening.
overlaps: ACX-17, ACX-22, SDX-07

title: Single authoritative policy decision
invariant: Sensitive branching consumes one request-scoped authoritative policy decision, or an equivalent server-side decision over the same complete tuple.
attackerControl: The caller influences client capabilities, UI state, feature flags, request booleans, cached decisions, metadata-only annotations, or a secondary policy result.
differential: Route security uses an authoritative engine, while a deeper branch trusts a weaker, stale, differently scoped, undefined, or non-enforcing signal.
requiredProof: Establish the semantics of both decision sources, show how they diverge for a reachable caller, and trace the weaker branch to protected output or effect.
decisiveRejection: The branch consumes the authoritative result or recomputes an equivalent fail-closed check against the same current principal, action, resource, scope, and representation.
overlaps: ACX-06, ACX-07, ACX-17

title: Security-sensitive field and value assignment
invariant: Every protected field or value is assignable only by a caller authorized to grant that exact effective role, scope, ownership, tenant, status, capability, or security consequence.
attackerControl: The caller supplies direct, nested, merged, imported, defaulted, aliased, or alternate-representation fields whose values influence authority or protected state.
differential: The guard authorizes object creation or update in general, while binding, deserialization, merge, model, or persistence code accepts a security-sensitive field or a value above the caller's grantable ceiling.
requiredProof: Trace the attacker-controlled field through every allowlist and transformation, show the effective persisted or executed value, and demonstrate a protected state or authority the caller cannot assign through the secure sibling.
decisiveRejection: An explicit schema excludes protected fields by default and an authoritative field-and-value policy validates every effective assignment, including nested, bulk, import, and alternate representations.
overlaps: ACX-02, ACX-20, ACX-30, PDX-07

title: Authorization before every terminal branch
invariant: No success, no-op, duplicate, unchanged, already-complete, validation-error, or other terminal branch can return protected data or perform an effect before authorization.
attackerControl: The caller selects values that trigger an early return, short circuit, special error, equality condition, or idempotent branch.
differential: The handler resolves a protected object, branches before the secure sibling's policy check, and then serializes the object or commits a side effect.
requiredProof: Prove the pre-branch lookup is unscoped, the branch precedes every equivalent authorization layer, and the terminal path exposes protected data or performs a forbidden action.
decisiveRejection: Authorization precedes resource-dependent branching, the lookup is already scoped, or the terminal response and effects contain no protected resource information.
overlaps: ACX-01, ACX-17, SMX-01

title: Unauthorized existence and metadata confidentiality
invariant: Callers denied a resource cannot learn protected existence, state, relationships, or other sensitive metadata through distinguishable behavior.
attackerControl: The caller varies identifiers, relationship targets, action parameters, or probes that distinguish missing, forbidden, invalid-state, or conflicting resources.
differential: The secure read path hides unauthorized objects, while an action, validation, timing, count, status, or error path resolves the object before applying equivalent concealment.
requiredProof: Demonstrate a reliable distinguishable signal, a realistic enumeration or targeting path, and why the disclosed fact crosses an intended confidentiality boundary.
decisiveRejection: Unauthorized and nonexistent cases are intentionally indistinguishable at the observable boundary, or the inferred fact is public and yields no protected information.
overlaps: ACX-17, SDX-08

title: Current authority and lifecycle revalidation
invariant: Deferred work, derived copies, synchronized replicas, cached grants, and child capabilities stop honoring authority or object state that has been revoked, suspended, archived, deleted, or otherwise invalidated.
attackerControl: The attacker queues work, retains a derived artifact or token, primes a cache, or invokes an alternate path before or after an authority or lifecycle change.
differential: Authorization is captured at creation or enqueue time, while the later sink uses stale identity, membership, source visibility, lifecycle state, or parent capability validity.
requiredProof: Establish the invalidating event, trace the stale authority to later consumption, and demonstrate protected access or effect after the intended revocation boundary.
decisiveRejection: The design explicitly grants a bounded immutable snapshot, or consumption checks current authority and lifecycle state and invalidates every dependent cache, copy, task, and capability.
overlaps: ACX-07, ACX-09, ACX-13, CBX-05, QEX-06

title: Authentic acting identity and delegation chain
invariant: Acting identity and impersonation are derived from authenticated, authorized, integrity-protected delegation rather than mutable object attributes or caller claims.
attackerControl: The attacker influences author, owner, committer, initiator, subject, run-as, forwarded identity, imported metadata, impersonation target, or delegation duration.
differential: The guard authenticates one principal, while token issuance or execution selects another identity from attacker-controlled or weakly verified data and applies the wrong privilege set.
requiredProof: Trace the identity selection and delegation chain, prove the attacker can control or obtain the resulting identity, and demonstrate an authority gain at a sensitive sink.
decisiveRejection: Each delegation hop authenticates the delegator, authorizes the target and scope, prevents upward delegation, binds audience and expiry, and applies the intended least-privilege identity.
overlaps: ACX-05, ACX-06, ACX-30, QEX-02, RIX-04

title: Relationship transition authority
invariant: Move, transfer, share, assign, parent, ownership, membership, and inheritance changes authorize the source, destination, relationship, and resulting effective authority.
attackerControl: The caller selects source and destination objects, parent or owner identifiers, membership roles, labels, namespaces, or relationship types.
differential: The guard checks only one endpoint or the pre-transition object, while the sink writes another relationship whose inherited policy grants access or influence the caller may not create.
requiredProof: Resolve both endpoints and the post-transition authority graph, identify the missing source, destination, relationship, or grant check, and demonstrate unauthorized state or privilege.
decisiveRejection: One atomic policy decision covers read/remove authority on the source, create/write authority on the destination, the relationship itself, and all effective post-transition grants.
overlaps: ACX-14, ACX-20, ACX-29, SMX-01

title: Atomic authorization and mutation
invariant: Security predicates and the mutations they authorize are evaluated over one consistent state or protected by equivalent concurrency control.
attackerControl: The attacker races authorization-relevant membership, ownership, balance, lifecycle, version, relationship, or resource state between check and use.
differential: The guard approves an earlier snapshot or transaction, while the sink commits against a later state in which the predicate is false or the protected invariant has changed.
requiredProof: Identify the interleaving, state transition, and missing lock, version predicate, transactional isolation, or atomic conditional write, then show a forbidden committed result.
decisiveRejection: The check and mutation are atomic over the relevant rows and external effects, or optimistic concurrency and retry recompute the complete authorization predicate before commit.
overlaps: ACX-10, ACX-20, ACX-28, SMX-03

title: Delegated authority ceiling
invariant: Creating, rotating, exchanging, or delegating a role, token, service identity, child capability, or custom permission cannot exceed the delegator's grantable authority.
attackerControl: The caller selects role, access level, scopes, audience, subject, resource, lifetime, or child credential parameters.
differential: The guard checks permission to manage or mint the delegated object, while the sink grants scopes, roles, duration, or targets broader than the caller may assign.
requiredProof: Compare the delegator's grantable authority with the issued credential's effective authority and demonstrate a protected operation newly available through the delegate.
decisiveRejection: Issuance enforces a non-escalating authority lattice, restricts grantable scopes and lifetime, binds the resource and audience, and preserves revocation through the full chain.
overlaps: ACX-05, ACX-09, ACX-26, ACX-27

title: Accountable privileged-action provenance
invariant: Every security-sensitive path records immutable, accurate actor, subject, delegation, action, resource, and result provenance that the acting principal cannot suppress or rewrite.
attackerControl: The caller selects an alternate interface, worker path, impersonation mode, batch route, or audit-record mutation that changes or omits accountability data.
differential: The canonical path emits protected audit evidence, while an equivalent path omits it, attributes the wrong principal, records only partial context, or permits the actor to alter the record.
requiredProof: Trace the same sensitive effect through both paths, establish the audit obligation as a security control, and show a reachable omission, misattribution, or unauthorized record mutation.
decisiveRejection: A trusted boundary emits append-only records for every equivalent path with complete actor and delegation context, and the acting principal cannot disable or modify them.
overlaps: ACX-19, ACX-27, QEX-01

title: Authorized state-machine transitions
invariant: Each security-sensitive state transition validates the current actor, immutable operation semantics, predecessor state, replay status, and target at the transition that commits the effect.
attackerControl: The caller skips or reorders steps, replays a request, modifies amount or destination between stages, changes an approved object, or invokes an alternate transition.
differential: An earlier step authorizes one state or semantic payload, while a later transition commits different, stale, replayed, or otherwise unauthorized semantics.
requiredProof: Reconstruct the state machine, identify the missing transition predicate or binding, and demonstrate a committed protected result the caller cannot obtain through the canonical flow.
decisiveRejection: Every transition atomically verifies current authority, predecessor state, immutable semantics, freshness, and idempotency before external and persistent effects.
overlaps: ACX-10, ACX-13, ACX-29, SMX-01, SMX-02, SMX-06

title: Passkey ceremony binding failure
invariant: Registration and authentication must bind a fresh challenge, relying party, origin, ceremony type, credential, account, user-presence or verification requirement, algorithm policy, and explicit authenticator-state policy.
attackerControl: Ceremony response, credential identifier, client data, authenticator data, user handle, transport, account selector, replay timing, or enrollment path.
differential: A scoped ceremony is initiated, but the verifier accepts a response from another origin, relying party, account, tenant, ceremony, challenge, or assurance level.
requiredProof: Trace challenge creation, storage, verification, consumption, and credential lookup, then show an attacker-supplied response is accepted for unintended account authority.
decisiveRejection: The effective verifier enforces the full tuple, consumes challenges atomically, applies an explicit counter or cloned-authenticator policy, and no alternate enrollment or login path weakens it.
overlaps: Cryptographic verification, parser differentials, ATX-02, ATX-16.

title: Authentication assurance downgrade
invariant: Every path that creates or upgrades equivalent account authority must enforce the required factors, confirmation state, and step-up assurance.
attackerControl: Login route, grant type, recovery or support flow, legacy or mobile API, SSO callback, magic link, API token, fallback factor, or sensitive operation.
differential: The primary ceremony enforces stronger assurance while an alternate path issues the same session, token, account access, or sensitive state transition with weaker checks.
requiredProof: Compare two reachable paths to the same effective authority and identify the exact required factor, state, or reauthentication check absent from the weaker path.
decisiveRejection: A central server-side policy derives the required assurance from the resulting authority and rejects every route whose verified ceremony is insufficient.
overlaps: ACX-02/09, ATX-07, ATX-10, cross-channel policy drift.

title: Federated and linked identity confusion
invariant: OAuth, OIDC, SAML, social login, invitations, and account linking must bind one intended issuer, client, tenant, redirect, transaction, subject, and verified identity claim.
attackerControl: Authorization response, state, nonce, PKCE values, redirect, issuer choice, assertion, external subject, email or phone claim, invitation, provider account, or link target.
differential: One component validates a signature or callback while account selection trusts a claim, transaction, issuer, redirect, or external identifier that was not bound to that validated ceremony.
requiredProof: Trace the verified response through identity lookup or linking and show attacker-controlled federated data resolves to, links with, or authenticates as a different account or tenant.
decisiveRejection: State and nonce are fresh and consumed, PKCE and exact redirect are enforced where applicable, issuer and audience are pinned, and only provider-verified stable identifiers select accounts.
overlaps: ATX-02, ATX-04, request integrity, XML and token verification.

title: Device authorization transaction confusion
invariant: Device code, user code, client, tenant, approving identity, displayed device context, scope, expiry, polling state, and issued credential must describe one immutable transaction.
attackerControl: Device or user code, client identifier, requested scope, tenant, approval session, polling client, race timing, or device description.
differential: The user approves one displayed transaction while polling, lookup, or issuance resolves a different device, client, tenant, scope, or identity.
requiredProof: Follow both browser and device branches through shared state and demonstrate code substitution, cross-client polling, approval race, or issuance outside the approved tuple.
decisiveRejection: High-entropy expiring codes map atomically to one transaction, approval shows and binds security-relevant context, polling is client-bound, and issuance consumes the transaction once.
overlaps: ATX-03, ATX-16, state-machine races, transaction substitution.

title: Refresh-token family replay
invariant: Rotation and revocation must make a refresh-token family single-use, race-safe, and unable to outlive its parent session, account, tenant, or authorization state.
attackerControl: Old or concurrent refresh token, rotation timing, logout or revocation sequence, client instance, family identifier, or child-token request.
differential: One token is revoked or rotated while a replay, concurrent winner, descendant, sibling, or independently cached credential remains accepted.
requiredProof: Reconstruct the family graph and atomic update order, then show a stale or replayed member yields a usable credential after the governing state should reject it.
decisiveRejection: Rotation is atomic, reuse triggers bounded family revocation, descendants inherit lifecycle state, and every issuance rechecks current account and authorization status.
overlaps: ATX-08, replay, distributed invalidation, time-of-check/time-of-use.

title: Primary identifier change takeover
invariant: Changing an email, phone, username, or other recovery identifier must bind the current account, sufficient reauthentication, destination verification, uniqueness, notification, and session lifecycle.
attackerControl: New identifier, current session, confirmation link, account or tenant selector, concurrent change, stale session, or recovery initiation after the change.
differential: An update endpoint can commit a recovery-capable identifier or activate it through a confirmation detached from the initiating account, authority, or pending value.
requiredProof: Trace request, pending state, confirmation, uniqueness enforcement, notifications, and session effects, then show the attacker gains durable login or recovery control.
decisiveRejection: Strong reauthentication, transaction-bound confirmation, database-enforced uniqueness, old-destination notification, race-safe activation, and appropriate session invalidation all hold.
overlaps: ATX-07, ATX-16, account recovery, identifier races.

title: One-time authentication and recovery token binding
invariant: Magic links, reset tokens, confirmations, and recovery artifacts must be unpredictable, purpose-bound, account-bound, destination-bound where relevant, expiring, and atomically single-use.
attackerControl: Token input, token-generation timing, account identifier, purpose, host or forwarded metadata, redirect, client or device context, concurrent redemption, or password-change sequence.
differential: Generation protects one representation or lifecycle state while construction, decoding, lookup, or redemption drops identity, purpose, destination, expiry, entropy, or consumption guarantees.
requiredProof: Trace randomness, stored representation, URL construction, lookup, expiry, use, and invalidation and demonstrate prediction, replay, cross-purpose use, host poisoning, or wrong-account redemption.
decisiveRejection: Cryptographic randomness, canonical construction, narrow tuple binding, constant-time comparison where material, atomic consumption, short expiry, and invalidation on relevant account changes are enforced.
overlaps: ATX-02, ATX-06, request-host trust, representation differentials.

title: Session and federation lifecycle divergence
invariant: Local sessions, federated sessions, derived credentials, concurrent-session policy, idle or absolute timeouts, role changes, tenant changes, logout, and deprovisioning must share the intended lifecycle.
attackerControl: Existing session or token, alternate channel, WebSocket or long-lived connection, IdP logout, SCIM event, password or role change, device session, or concurrency timing.
differential: One channel records revocation, timeout, logout, deprovisioning, or session replacement while another independently usable session, connection, cache, or credential is not checked or invalidated.
requiredProof: Identify the authoritative lifecycle event and all consumers, then show a credential or connection continues to perform a protected operation after that event completes.
decisiveRejection: Consumers revalidate current lifecycle state or receive verified complete invalidation, and any documented grace window cannot yield authority beyond policy.
overlaps: ATX-05, cache invalidation, asynchronous propagation, stale authorization.

title: Trusted-device credential transfer
invariant: Remembered-device and persistent-login credentials must have sufficient entropy, narrow account and purpose binding, bounded lifetime, rotation, revocation, and the intended device or key possession property.
attackerControl: Trusted-device token or cookie, device identifier, enrollment path, copied storage, password or MFA-reset sequence, replay device, or recovery flow.
differential: Interactive MFA or login is device-scoped, but a clonable bearer artifact grants the same bypass from another context or survives a security reset.
requiredProof: Trace issuance, storage, verification, binding, expiry, and invalidation and show transfer or replay grants authentication assurance not otherwise available.
decisiveRejection: The credential is cryptographically bound to non-exportable device possession or an explicitly accepted bearer model with narrow scope, rotation, expiry, and complete security-event revocation.
overlaps: ATX-02, ATX-08, client storage, stolen-token replay.

title: Support and impersonation identity confusion
invariant: Support recovery, account merge, impersonation, and administrative identity operations must resolve one intended account and tenant, require commensurate step-up, constrain delegated authority, and preserve accountable audit context.
attackerControl: Search identifier, customer-supplied evidence, merge source or destination, impersonation target, tenant, recovery channel, support workflow state, or operator-facing metadata.
differential: An operator or service is authorized to assist one identity, but ambiguous lookup, mutable evidence, detached approval, or broad execution credentials select or alter another identity.
requiredProof: Trace attacker influence through the support or merge decision to the exact account mutation or impersonation grant and demonstrate an authority delta or durable takeover.
decisiveRejection: Stable identifiers, tenant-scoped lookup, independent verified evidence, step-up, immutable approval binding, least-privilege delegation, and tamper-resistant attribution cover the complete operation.
overlaps: ACX-05/12, ATX-03, ATX-06, approval substitution.

title: Account discovery and recovery oracle
invariant: Unauthenticated or weakly authorized authentication and recovery responses must not reveal protected account existence or lifecycle facts beyond an accepted disclosure policy.
attackerControl: Username, email, phone, external identifier, reset or registration request, response branch, timing observation, or repeated bounded probes.
differential: Direct account lookup is protected while status, body, timing, delivery behavior, error metadata, or a downstream side effect distinguishes registered or sensitive account state.
requiredProof: Define the protected fact and observation model, control confounders, and show practical reliable distinction within realistic query volume and program scope.
decisiveRejection: The fact is intentionally public, responses and relevant side effects are indistinguishable, or noise and required volume make inference impractical or out of scope.
overlaps: SDX-08, registration privacy, timing side channels.

title: Privilege-transition session fixation
invariant: A session identifier or equivalent bearer handle known before authentication or privilege elevation must not remain the handle for the resulting stronger authority.
attackerControl: Pre-authentication session, session cookie or handle, login link, fixation channel, authentication timing, MFA completion, role elevation, or password-change flow.
differential: Credentials or a second factor are verified correctly, but the stronger authenticated state is attached to an attacker-known or lower-assurance session handle.
requiredProof: Establish attacker knowledge or control of the pre-transition handle and show the identical usable handle survives a real authority transition.
decisiveRejection: The server rotates the handle and invalidates the old state atomically at every relevant transition, with cookies and channel bindings preventing fixation.
overlaps: Session lifecycle, ATX-02, token replay.

title: Authentication attempt and lockout control divergence
invariant: Password, OTP, recovery, token-validation, and batch authentication attempts must share server-side abuse controls keyed to trustworthy accountable dimensions without enabling trivial victim lockout.
attackerControl: Alternate endpoint, credential type, identifier spelling, batch size, GraphQL alias, client or proxy metadata, concurrency, failure class, or reset sequence.
differential: One route or representation enforces bounded attempts while another reaches the same verifier outside accounting, resets counters incorrectly, amplifies guesses, or lets unauthenticated input impose disproportionate lockout.
requiredProof: Identify the effective counter and trusted key, quantify a realistic attack under program scope, and demonstrate practical credential compromise or accepted security impact rather than a generic missing-rate-limit claim.
decisiveRejection: Central accounting covers equivalent attempts, batch work is charged per credential, spoofable metadata is not trusted, atomic state prevents races, and remaining attack requires excluded high-volume or third-party compromise.
overlaps: Resource exhaustion, ATX-02, OTP replay, availability policy.

title: Server-side credential policy bypass
invariant: Every server path that creates or changes a password or equivalent user-managed credential must enforce the authoritative policy and current-account requirements.
attackerControl: Direct API or RPC request, alternate serializer, import or bulk path, credential-change flow, policy field, legacy client, or validation ordering.
differential: A client, primary route, or preflight enforces credential policy while an alternate server path persists a credential that the authoritative policy should reject.
requiredProof: Reach the production credential store through the weaker path and show the resulting credential changes security posture or enables a concrete accepted attack.
decisiveRejection: One server-side validator governs every write path, datastore constraints cover critical invariants, and the observed difference is cosmetic or has no accepted security impact.
overlaps: ATX-02, bulk/import differentials, policy drift.

title: Token verifier and claim binding failure
invariant: Signed or encrypted authentication tokens must use pinned algorithms and trusted keys and must validate issuer, audience, subject, tenant, purpose, time, key identifier, and authorization claims for the consuming service.
attackerControl: Token, header, algorithm, key identifier or lookup input, claims, key source, token type, issuer, audience, expiry representation, or alternate verifier path.
differential: Cryptographic parsing or signature verification succeeds while attacker-influenced key selection, algorithm negotiation, claim trust, token-type confusion, or inconsistent verifier policy grants unintended identity or authority.
requiredProof: Trace the exact production verifier and key resolution and show a forged, confused, or mis-scoped token is accepted at a protected sink with concrete authority.
decisiveRejection: Algorithms and key sources are pinned, dangerous modes are rejected, all consumer-specific claims are validated, and authorization is derived from trusted current state where required.
overlaps: Cryptographic misuse, ATX-03, parser differentials, authorization claims.

title: Atomic identity claim and one-time transition
invariant: Registration, invitation acceptance, identity linking, uniqueness claims, and other one-time account transitions must be database-enforced, transaction-bound, and atomically consumed.
attackerControl: Concurrent requests, email or username, invitation or transition token, tenant, case or Unicode variant, source and destination account, or retry timing.
differential: Application code checks availability or unused state before a separate write, allowing concurrent or canonically equivalent operations to claim the same identity or consume one transition more than once.
requiredProof: Trace canonicalization, transaction boundaries, datastore constraints, and retry behavior and demonstrate a race that yields duplicate ownership, wrong-account activation, or multiple successful consumption.
decisiveRejection: Canonical uniqueness and conditional consumption are enforced atomically by the authoritative store and conflict or retry paths fail closed without partial account state.
overlaps: ATX-03/06/07, state-machine races, datastore uniqueness.

title: Untrusted context becomes instruction
invariant: Content from an untrusted author must remain data and must not become authority-bearing instructions for a protected action.
attackerControl: Retrieved documents, pages, messages, files, tool output, or other context authored by `C` and supplied to the model.
differential: Ingress treats the context as data, but prompt construction lets its text compete with trusted instructions and select tool or data behavior.
requiredProof: Show `C` controls production-reachable content, the model follows it sufficiently to reach a protected tool or data sink, and deterministic policy does not stop the action.
decisiveRejection: Downstream authorization and typed tool policy make model text non-authoritative for the resolved operation.
overlaps: Prompt injection, AIX-05/08/10/11, tool authorization, retrieval boundaries.

title: Forged trusted conversation state
invariant: System, assistant, function-call, approval, and tool-result states must be server-created or integrity-bound to the exact run.
attackerControl: Client-submitted message roles, conversation history, function-call records, approval markers, tool results, and run identifiers.
differential: The API accepts client-originated records but downstream orchestration treats them as model-, server-, tool-, or approver-authored state.
requiredProof: Demonstrate acceptance of the forged transition and show it changes protected tool execution, data access, approval state, or conversation authority.
decisiveRejection: Trusted states are created server-side and integrity-bound to the run, actor, ordering, and state transition before use.
overlaps: ACX-08, state-machine bypass, signed-message integrity, replay.

title: Declared tool and resolved operation diverge
invariant: Authorization must derive from the authoritative resolved tool, account, target, operation, and exact arguments used at execution.
attackerControl: Tool name, connector or account identifier, operation discriminator, target, arguments, and registry lookup inputs.
differential: A generic router validates a declared name or schema while runtime identifiers resolve another tool, account, connector, or forbidden operation.
requiredProof: Show the declared and resolved tuples differ, or trace attacker-controlled arguments to a protected action outside the approved tuple.
decisiveRejection: Policy loads the authoritative object first and binds the resolved tool, identity, target, operation, and normalized arguments before execution.
overlaps: ACX-11, XD-04/17, dynamic dispatch, connector and plugin resolution.

title: Retrieval drops tenant or document authority
invariant: Every retrieval, reranking, cache, fallback, and citation-fetch stage must preserve tenant, owner, classification, and document-level access control.
attackerControl: Query text, embedding input, identifiers, namespace selectors, filters, fallback conditions, and cache keys available to the requester.
differential: An early retrieval stage is scoped, but a later search, rerank, cache hit, fallback, or citation load omits an authority dimension.
requiredProof: Identify the stage that drops scope and show out-of-authority content reaches the requesting user or model-accessible context.
decisiveRejection: Final retrieval and every fallback, cache, reranker, and citation resolver intersect results with current authoritative access.
overlaps: ACX-07, cache isolation, search-strategy scope, sensitive-data disclosure.

title: Tool output reaches a second active sink
invariant: Tool, page, plugin, and service output must remain provenance-labeled untrusted data at every later parser and active sink.
attackerControl: Output of a tool or external content source that the attacker can influence directly or through stored data.
differential: The first tool treats output as data, but orchestration later interpolates it into a URL, command, code, query, template, parser, or approval display.
requiredProof: Trace output provenance and transformations through the second sink and demonstrate the protected operation or misleading approval semantics it controls.
decisiveRejection: Typed schemas, context-correct encoding, provenance handling, and independent sink authorization preserve the output as inert data.
overlaps: Second-order injection, SSRF, command/query injection, AIX-01/07/11.

title: Durable agent-memory poisoning
invariant: Long-term memory and shared agent state must preserve author, tenant, provenance, expiry, and authority and be reauthorized at every later use.
attackerControl: Content writable into memory, profiles, instructions, retrieval stores, summaries, or shared state and attributes that influence later selection.
differential: A low-authority write is stored as durable trusted context and later selected in another session, tenant, user, or authority context.
requiredProof: Show attacker write access, durable persistence, later selection, the victim or authority change, and a concrete protected effect.
decisiveRejection: Owner and tenant scope, provenance labels, expiry, isolation, and safe reauthorization prevent cross-context authoritative reuse.
overlaps: Stored injection, AIX-01/04/05, cache poisoning, cross-tenant state.

title: Approval and execution semantic drift
invariant: Human approval must cover the immutable canonical tool, target, arguments, side effects, credential, and execution version.
attackerControl: Hidden, defaulted, truncated, encoded, late-resolved, or mutable tool arguments and data used to render an approval summary.
differential: The approval interface displays or summarizes one operation while runtime resolution or mutation executes another semantic tuple.
requiredProof: Record and compare the canonical approved tuple and executed tuple, including credential and side effects, and show the difference crosses authority.
decisiveRejection: Approval binds an immutable fully resolved tuple and execution rejects any post-approval difference.
overlaps: XD-03/09, ACX-09/10, TOCTOU, UI redressing and transaction signing.

title: Agent credential and authority laundering
invariant: Every tool effect must be bounded by the accountable trigger's authority, an immutable operation-scoped delegation, or an explicit deterministic system-owned service policy for the exact resolved operation.
attackerControl: Agent instructions, trigger inputs, tool selection, targets, arguments, connector selection, browser actions, and untrusted content that influences the model-produced invocation.
differential: Agent-authored behavior executes using `E`, whose connector, service, session, key, or operator authority exceeds both the authenticated trigger's grant and any deterministic policy intended to constrain a system-owned agent.
requiredProof: Identify exact `U` and `E`, distinguish interactive from intentionally system-owned execution, compare semantic authority and service policy, and show attacker-controlled input selects a forbidden operation-bound dimension.
decisiveRejection: Current trigger authority, a valid immutable delegation, or deterministic non-model service policy constrains the exact resolved tool effect even when the technical credential is broader or the agent is system initiated.
overlaps: ACX-05/06, XD-05/20, confused deputy, connector and delegated execution.

title: Autonomous loop and fan-out amplification
invariant: Enforce cost, action, recursion, retry, and fan-out budgets before every autonomous step and delegated task.
attackerControl: Prompts, retrieved task graphs, tool output, retry-triggering responses, recursive delegation, and inputs affecting branching or termination.
differential: An outer request appears bounded while nested model/tool loops, retries, delegation, or parallel tasks consume unbounded shared resources or actions.
requiredProof: Quantify per-level budgets, branching, retries, termination, attacker cost, and the affected shared resource or protected action set.
decisiveRejection: Hard cumulative budgets are enforced before every action, or work is bounded, isolated, and charged entirely to the authorized requester without shared impact.
overlaps: XD-13/14, resource exhaustion, queue amplification, recursive workflow execution.

title: Model output used as authoritative policy
invariant: Authorization and safety decisions for protected sinks must be deterministic and authoritative outside model output.
attackerControl: Prompts, context, examples, tool output, or other input that influences a model classification, confidence, or policy response.
differential: A model classification, prompt rule, or self-reported confidence directly allows a protected operation without a deterministic policy decision.
requiredProof: Trace the model-controlled value to the final gate and show an attacker can influence it to select the forbidden sink behavior.
decisiveRejection: Deterministic server policy reauthorizes the resolved operation and model output can only propose or describe actions.
overlaps: AIX-01/08, access control, content moderation boundaries, confused deputy.

title: Cross-modal instruction smuggling
invariant: Every modality supplied to a model must be represented as untrusted context in approval, provenance, and downstream tool policy.
attackerControl: Images, optical text, audio, metadata, attachments, rendered pages, encoded fields, and transformations that reveal hidden instructions.
differential: The security or approval layer inspects one representation while a production modality parser supplies additional instruction-bearing content to the model.
requiredProof: Pin the real modality extraction path and show hidden attacker content changes a protected tool, data, or approval outcome not independently blocked.
decisiveRejection: All modalities are provenance-labeled untrusted context and every resulting tool effect remains independently authorized.
overlaps: PDX-05, AIX-01/05/07, content classification, hidden-input differentials.

title: Secret-bearing context disclosure
invariant: Secrets and other users' private context must not enter model-accessible state or outputs beyond the requester's explicit authority.
attackerControl: Prompts, retrieval queries, debug options, conversation identifiers, output requests, and content that influences context selection or model response.
differential: A system prompt, retrieved record, credential, hidden execution data, or another conversation enters model/debug context and can be emitted to the requester.
requiredProof: Identify the real secret, prove it is present in accessible context, and demonstrate an attacker-observable output or debug channel.
decisiveRejection: The value never enters requester-accessible model context, or deterministic output and debug controls prevent disclosure on the exact path.
overlaps: Sensitive-data exposure, AIX-04/06, debug endpoints, logs and conversation isolation.

title: Trusted Types policy and gadget bypass
invariant: Trusted Types policies and equivalent safe-value abstractions must accept only representations proven safe for the exact HTML, script, or URL sink they authorize.
attackerControl: Policy input, policy name or selection, default policy, wrapper object, DOM gadget input, script URL, template output, or policy-creation path.
differential: A type or policy label is trusted while a permissive transformer, confused safe-value kind, attacker-selectable policy, or existing gadget produces executable content.
requiredProof: Trace attacker bytes through the effective policy to an enforced active sink and demonstrate supported-browser execution under the deployed policy configuration.
decisiveRejection: Policy creation is fixed and least-privileged, transformations are context-specific, attacker input cannot select a gadget, and enforcement blocks every untyped alternate sink.
overlaps: XX-05/07/14, sanitizer policy, type confusion.

title: DOM name and property clobbering
invariant: Security-sensitive DOM lookups and control flow must not resolve attacker-created named elements or inherited browser properties in place of expected objects or values.
attackerControl: Element names or identifiers, document structure, form controls, collection entries, global property names, markup location, or parser-created relationships.
differential: Code assumes an own program-defined value while browser named-property resolution substitutes an attacker-created node or collection that later controls a URL, script, form, sanitizer, or decision.
requiredProof: Show the supported browser's actual property resolution and trace the substituted value to an active sink or protected state change.
decisiveRejection: Lookups use lexical bindings, explicit selectors with type checks, own-property-safe structures, and no attacker markup can introduce a colliding name on the path.
overlaps: XX-11, DOM parser behavior, object-property confusion.

title: Browser channel authenticity and capability confusion
invariant: Messages must bind expected origin, source browsing context or endpoint, channel, schema, transaction, object capability, and authorized target action.
attackerControl: Message data, sender origin or window, opener or frame relationship, channel identifier, transferred object, action, target origin, timing, or reply endpoint.
differential: A listener validates only message shape or origin while source context, transaction, capability, or destination remains substitutable and drives an active sink or privileged browser action.
requiredProof: Establish a realistic attacker-controlled sender, pass the deployed checks, and trace the accepted message to execution, secret disclosure, navigation, or a protected state change.
decisiveRejection: Exact origin and source are pinned, schemas reject ambiguity, transactions and capabilities are unforgeable and scoped, and replies use an exact trusted destination.
overlaps: Request integrity, confused deputies, XX-06/09.

title: Serialized state and hydration grammar breakout
invariant: Server state must be encoded for every grammar it crosses and hydration must consume the same trusted representation and policy as the server render.
attackerControl: Serialized field, property name, closing delimiter, Unicode separator, initial-state blob, hydration source, client refetch, component boundary, or mismatch-triggering state.
differential: Data is safe for JSON or server HTML in isolation but concatenation, script embedding, attribute placement, template literals, client parsing, or hydration reinterprets it in a more powerful grammar.
requiredProof: Reconstruct the exact emitted bytes and client hydration path and demonstrate execution in a supported browser, including the deployed encoder and Content Security Policy.
decisiveRejection: Context-correct serialization prevents delimiter breakout, inert data containers are used, hydration consumes the same safe representation, and mismatches cannot select an active sink.
overlaps: XX-13/14, parser differentials, server-side rendering.

title: Content Security Policy trust failure
invariant: Nonces, hashes, allowed sources, and trusted loaders must authorize only immutable intended script and must not turn attacker-controlled data or hosting into executable code.
attackerControl: Injection point, nonce observation, nonced element content, allowed-host path, script-loader argument, JSONP or callback input, module specifier, base URL, or cached response.
differential: Policy blocks ordinary inline execution while a nonce-bearing container, reusable nonce, trusted loader, allowed origin, or script gadget converts attacker data into code.
requiredProof: Use the deployed policy and supported browser to trace a reachable injection through the specific trusted source or gadget to execution; a broad directive alone is insufficient.
decisiveRejection: Nonces are per response and unexposed, trusted script content is immutable, allowed origins cannot host attacker-controlled executable responses, and no reachable loader evaluates attacker input.
overlaps: XX-01/06/07, supply-chain hosting, cache poisoning.

title: Executable navigation and URL interpretation
invariant: User-influenced navigation and URL-bearing sinks must permit only intended schemes, origins, resource types, and execution contexts after canonical parsing.
attackerControl: URL, scheme, host, base URL, redirect, fragment, encoding, protocol-relative form, blob or data construction, source document, window target, or framework navigation object.
differential: Validation examines a string, prefix, host-like fragment, or pre-decoded form while the browser resolves a different executable scheme, origin, base, document, or resource context.
requiredProof: Identify the effective browser URL parser and sink and show the accepted canonical URL executes code or exposes protected browser authority under deployed controls.
decisiveRejection: A canonical parser enforces a narrow scheme and origin allowlist, rejects ambiguous inputs, and the selected element or API cannot execute the accepted resource type.
overlaps: SSRF, open redirect chaining, XX-08/13, parser differentials.

title: Interpreted template and expression injection
invariant: Attacker-controlled data must remain data and never become template source, expression syntax, component identity, directive, markdown extension, module specifier, or evaluated code.
attackerControl: Template or markdown content, expression, directive, component name, helper, renderer option, dynamic import, compilation flag, plugin, or extension configuration.
differential: An input is escaped or sanitized as display data on one path while another renderer compiles, evaluates, extends, or treats it as structural syntax.
requiredProof: Trace the exact production renderer and enabled options and demonstrate that attacker-controlled syntax reaches an execution-capable construct in the supported client.
decisiveRejection: Templates and renderers are fixed, user values enter only typed data slots, raw or extension modes are disabled, and output receives context-correct sanitization before any active sink.
overlaps: Command/template injection, XX-01/12/14, markdown rendering.

title: Active-content preview and conversion escape
invariant: Untrusted files and generated documents must not execute with trusted-origin browser authority or give converters unintended file, credential, network, or host capabilities.
attackerControl: Uploaded or generated bytes, declared type, filename, preview route, conversion input, embedded resource, active document feature, response headers, or navigation context.
differential: Upload validation or content labeling accepts a passive representation while preview, sniffing, inline serving, same-origin rendering, office or PDF conversion, or insufficient sandboxing activates a different representation.
requiredProof: Establish actual stored bytes, response headers, origin, element or converter, sandbox, and supported viewer behavior, then demonstrate execution or a concrete protected converter capability.
decisiveRejection: Content is safely transformed or rasterized, served from an isolated origin or as attachment with correct type and no sniffing, and converters disable active content and restrict filesystem and network access.
overlaps: File upload, SSRF, command execution, XX-06/15.

title: Real-time and streamed rendering gap
invariant: WebSocket, server-sent event, notification, collaborative, terminal, log, and incremental model streams must apply the same contextual rendering policy as ordinary responses.
attackerControl: Stream record or token, event type, partial markup boundary, terminal control data, collaboration operation, notification field, broadcast channel, ordering, or reconnect state.
differential: Stored or request-response rendering is encoded or sanitized, but incremental assembly, alternate event handlers, optimistic updates, or broadcast consumers reach an active sink without equivalent controls.
requiredProof: Trace attacker data through the real server and client stream path, including chunk assembly and final DOM operation, and demonstrate supported-browser execution or protected-data disclosure.
decisiveRejection: Typed schemas, channel authorization, inert text rendering, context-aware incremental encoding, and final-sink sanitization cover every event and partial-state path.
overlaps: XX-03/14, asynchronous authorization, terminal injection.

title: Service-worker and browser-cache persistence
invariant: Only trusted immutable script may control a bounded service-worker scope, imports, updates, navigation responses, and cache entries under a protected origin.
attackerControl: Worker script or registration URL, scope, imported script, update response, cache key or value, navigation request, offline fallback, storage namespace, or registration timing.
differential: A transient upload, injection, cache write, or route response becomes a persistent origin-level execution capability through worker registration or attacker-controlled cached navigation content.
requiredProof: Trace registration and scope rules, script delivery, update policy, cache mutation, and a later victim navigation to persistent execution or response control.
decisiveRejection: Worker URLs and imports are immutable and trusted, scope is minimal, untrusted responses cannot populate executable navigation entries, and update and cache policy remove attacker control.
overlaps: Cache poisoning, XX-05/08, persistence after XSS.

title: Prototype and shared-default pollution to browser sink
invariant: Attacker-controlled property paths must not modify prototypes or shared defaults later trusted as HTML, script, URL, renderer, sanitizer, or component configuration.
attackerControl: Object keys, nested paths, merge source, query or body decoder output, constructor or prototype names, defaults object, clone behavior, or configuration overlay.
differential: One layer treats keys as ordinary data while a recursive merge or property lookup changes inherited or shared state consumed by a separate active browser sink.
requiredProof: Demonstrate the exact write to inherited or shared state, the later property read, and the concrete supported-browser sink reached by the polluted value.
decisiveRejection: Dangerous keys are rejected throughout parsing and merge, null-prototype or own-property access dominates, shared state is immutable, or no active sink consumes the property.
overlaps: XX-02/14, object injection, shared-state contamination.

title: Sanitizer policy and post-sanitization mutation
invariant: Sanitizer policy must match the final browser context and no later hook, attribute write, renderer option, plugin, or transformation may restore capabilities the policy removed.
attackerControl: Markup, element and attribute mix, protocol, namespace, sanitizer configuration, custom hook, plugin, allowlist extension, post-processing input, or render context.
differential: A sanitizer validates one policy or DOM tree while relaxed options, unsafe extensions, re-added fields, composition, or later mutation produces a more powerful tree at the active sink.
requiredProof: Capture the sanitized representation and every subsequent mutation and show the final supported-browser DOM executes or exposes protected data under the effective policy.
decisiveRejection: A maintained context-appropriate policy removes active capabilities, configuration is fixed, post-processing operates on safe typed values, and the final sink receives the verified representation unchanged.
overlaps: XX-01/07/14/15, parser differentials.

title: Decode and canonicalization order mismatch
invariant: Validation, encoding, and sanitization must operate on the same fully decoded canonical representation and grammar that the final browser sink consumes.
attackerControl: Percent or entity encoding, Unicode form, escape sequence, nested encoding, duplicate decode marker, text extraction, parser serialization, or alternate transport representation.
differential: A guard sees encoded or differently normalized text while a later decoder, entity resolver, text-to-HTML conversion, URL parser, or serializer reveals active syntax after the guard.
requiredProof: Record every transformation in order and the exact bytes or DOM values at guard and sink, then demonstrate execution in the deployed rendering context.
decisiveRejection: Inputs are decoded once to a canonical form before context-specific validation, transformations cannot introduce syntax afterward, and the final API treats the result as inert text.
overlaps: PDX-01/03, XX-04/06/12/15, representation differentials.

title: Contextual browser output failure
invariant: Attacker data must be encoded or sanitized for the exact final HTML text, attribute, URL, script, style, DOM, or framework sink and remain inert through all alternate renderers.
attackerControl: Reflected or stored field, object property, template slot, raw or safe-value marker, DOM API argument, serializer, email content, renderer choice, or administrative view.
differential: A framework's default escaping or one renderer is safe while a raw-output escape hatch, wrong-context encoder, safe-marking API, client rerender, or alternate template places the value into an active grammar.
requiredProof: Trace attacker input to the exact final sink and context and demonstrate supported-browser execution; for email or non-browser renderers, prove the real supported client permits active behavior.
decisiveRejection: Typed contextual output encoding covers every renderer and branch, raw escape hatches accept only trusted constants or verified safe values, and deployed policy prevents residual execution.
overlaps: XX-01/04/07/09/12, stored and reflected XSS.

title: Browser parser mutation and namespace differential
invariant: Sanitizers and generators must preserve safety when browser parsing, reparsing, fragment insertion, copy and paste, serialization, or HTML, SVG, and MathML namespace transitions mutate structure.
attackerControl: Misnested markup, namespace integration point, fragment context, foreign content, clipboard HTML, parser error recovery, DOM serialization, or insertion API.
differential: A guard reasons over one parse tree or namespace while the supported browser constructs a different active tree after mutation, adoption, reparsing, or context change.
requiredProof: Compare the guard's effective tree with the browser's final DOM in the exact insertion context and demonstrate an active node, attribute, URL, or script capability.
decisiveRejection: The sanitizer is proven for supported parser behavior and fragment context, risky namespaces are removed or inert, and no post-sanitization reparse changes the security-relevant tree.
overlaps: PDX-03/05, XX-08/12/13, mutation XSS.

title: Style-context injection and browser exfiltration
invariant: Attacker-controlled style data must not escape its property or selector context, load unauthorized resources, overlay sensitive controls, or create a practical protected-data observation channel.
attackerControl: Style value, property name, selector, stylesheet, theme, URL, custom property, injected rule, DOM attribute visible to selectors, or repeated observation endpoint.
differential: HTML or script sanitization succeeds while allowed style syntax, unsafe interpolation, selector power, resource loads, or layout effects cross the intended visual-only boundary.
requiredProof: Establish the exact supported-browser style grammar and observable network or UI effect and demonstrate practical sensitive-data inference or protected user action, not cosmetic modification alone.
decisiveRejection: Style input is constrained to typed safe values, selectors and resource URLs are not attacker-controlled, Content Security Policy blocks unintended loads, and no sensitive DOM state is selector-observable.
overlaps: Data-exfiltration side channels, UI redress, XX-06/14.

title: Key the complete security tuple
invariant: Cache equivalence must include every input that can change authorization, confidentiality, representation, or side effects.
attackerControl: Identity, tenant, role, object, method, origin, locale, content negotiation, query, feature state, or authorization result.
differential: The producer checks a complete tuple while the cache key omits or normalizes one dimension later varied by a consumer.
requiredProof: Construct two realistic requests that collide on the effective key but are not security-equivalent and show forbidden reuse.
decisiveRejection: No shared cache exists, or keying and final authorization include every response- and decision-varying dimension.
overlaps: XD-19, ACX-07, RIX-05, multi-tenant storage.

title: Align priming authority with consumption authority
invariant: An actor allowed to populate or refresh an entry must not control data or metadata later trusted by a more privileged consumer.
attackerControl: Cacheable request, upstream response, refresh trigger, miss handler, vary input, metadata, tag, or prewarming job.
differential: Low authority selects cached content, status, headers, or routing state while a victim request reuses it under stronger identity or trust.
requiredProof: Trace who can cause the stored value, which cache layer accepts it, and a victim path that consumes it without equivalent validation.
decisiveRejection: Only trusted producers can write entries, entries are scoped to producer authority, or consumers independently validate all security-relevant fields.
overlaps: Cache poisoning, response splitting, proxy boundaries, confused deputies.

title: Canonicalize keys and `Vary` semantics consistently
invariant: Every cache and origin must derive the same canonical key and variation set from request semantics.
attackerControl: Duplicate or encoded headers, path/query normalization, host, port, scheme, method, body, delimiter, case, or forwarding metadata.
differential: Edge, framework, application, and origin parse or normalize key material differently, causing distinct requests to alias or equivalent requests to split controls.
requiredProof: Identify each deployed parser/key builder and show a concrete semantic mismatch that changes protected content or routing.
decisiveRejection: One canonical request object drives security and caching, ambiguity is rejected, and `Vary` covers every supported representation dimension.
overlaps: PDX-01/03, RIX-04/07, request desynchronization.

title: Keep private responses out of broader caches
invariant: Responses containing user-, tenant-, credential-, or authorization-specific data must never enter a cache with broader readership.
attackerControl: Authenticated request, cookie or authorization header, personalized response, redirect, error, download, or partial response.
differential: Application authorization is correct, but cacheability defaults, surrogate policy, or ignored request headers allow a shared layer to store and replay the response.
requiredProof: Establish actual cache policy and readership, then show a protected response is stored and retrievable by a weaker principal.
decisiveRejection: Effective no-store/private policy, authenticated-request bypass, partitioned caching, and downstream authorization prevent shared reuse.
overlaps: Sensitive-data exposure, ACX-21, CDN/proxy configuration.

title: Invalidate on authority and object-state change
invariant: Cached data and decisions must not outlive revocation, role/ownership change, deletion, visibility change, or protected content mutation.
attackerControl: Previously authorized session, stale entry, object transfer, permission change, soft deletion, version update, or delayed invalidation event.
differential: Authorization is evaluated when populating the cache while later reads trust that result after the authoritative tuple changes.
requiredProof: Trace mutation-to-invalidation ordering across all layers and show stale access or state survives a completed security change.
decisiveRejection: Read-time authorization, immutable versioned keys, synchronous invalidation, or a proven bounded policy window preserves the intended lifecycle.
overlaps: Pattern 29, XD-09, token/session revocation, lifecycle bypass.

title: Fail closed for negative, error, and partial entries
