invariant: Misses, denials, lookup failures, timeouts, partial results, and malformed upstream responses must not become broader cached truth.
attackerControl: Induced error, authorization denial, transient absence, timeout, partial response, unsupported variant, or fallback result.
differential: Success paths preserve scope, while error or negative caching drops identity/tenant context, changes status semantics, or selects a permissive fallback.
requiredProof: Show the attacker can create the exceptional entry and a later protected consumer receives a broader result or useful oracle.
decisiveRejection: Exceptional states are not cached or use the same complete key, bounded lifetime, and authorization as successful entries.
overlaps: XD-18, existence oracles, fail-open authorization, availability.

title: Preserve policy across cache layers and purges
invariant: Browser, service worker, edge, proxy, application, datastore, and worker caches must agree on scope, lifetime, and invalidation.
attackerControl: Layer-specific header, purge key, tag, namespace, refresh event, stale-if-error mode, or bypass parameter.
differential: One layer purges or partitions correctly while another retains, widens, or reconstructs the same content under different rules.
requiredProof: Enumerate every production cache on the path and demonstrate the layer that serves forbidden or stale material.
decisiveRejection: End-to-end policy and versioning cover all layers, purge completion is verified, and no hidden fallback can serve older state.
overlaps: Distributed invalidation, service workers, deployment configuration.

title: Isolate capacity and eviction by accountable scope
invariant: Cache cardinality, entry size, refresh work, and eviction pressure must be bounded and charged to the actor or tenant causing them.
attackerControl: High-cardinality key material, large values, cache-busting variants, refresh triggers, tenant label, or long retention.
differential: Request rate is bounded but accepted inputs create unbounded entries or evict another scope's security-critical working set.
requiredProof: Quantify attacker-controlled cardinality/cost and show shared memory, storage, backend amplification, or cross-tenant eviction impact.
decisiveRejection: Hard cardinality/size/TTL quotas, admission policy, fair partitioning, and bounded refresh work isolate consumers.
overlaps: REX-07/08, telemetry cardinality, backend amplification.

title: Overbroad trust principal
invariant: A trust policy must bind assumption or invocation to the exact intended principal, workload, source, and external context.
attackerControl: An independently obtainable principal, subject claim, source resource, external identifier, or session context matched by the trust rule.
differential: A wildcard, broad principal, weak subject pattern, or missing source condition admits identities outside the intended trust set.
requiredProof: Construct the effective trust decision and show an attacker-obtainable principal can assume the identity or invoke the protected service.
decisiveRejection: Explicit denies and verified conditions bind the exact administrative domain, workload, source, subject, and required external context.
overlaps: ACX-03/04, token exchange, federation, delegated identity.

title: Effective-policy composition drift
invariant: The effective authorization graph must enforce the intended restriction across identity, resource, boundary, session, and inherited policy layers.
attackerControl: Principal selection, resource target, action, session context, and any policy or grant writable at the attacker's privilege.
differential: One policy layer appears restrictive while another resource policy, access list, grant, inheritance edge, or session rule permits the operation.
requiredProof: Apply the actual policy-composition semantics, including denies and conditions, and demonstrate a reachable effective allow for the forbidden operation.
decisiveRejection: A dominating deny or unavailable principal/resource prerequisite prevents the operation in the effective policy graph.
overlaps: Access control, CLX-01/03/10/12, policy inheritance and delegation.

title: Tenant scope missing from storage or keys
invariant: Tenant-local authority must resolve only tenant-local resource names, object keys, data partitions, queues, caches, artifacts, and encryption keys.
attackerControl: Tenant-scoped requests, resource identifiers, prefixes, object keys, aliases, or configuration used to resolve shared infrastructure.
differential: Authorization is tenant-local but the final global resource name or policy omits the authoritative tenant dimension.
requiredProof: Trace the authorized tenant, final resolved resource/key, effective policy, and concrete cross-tenant read, write, action, or cryptographic effect.
decisiveRejection: Policy conditions and the final resolved key or resource identity include the authoritative tenant and cannot be overridden.
overlaps: ACX-04, XD-06, storage isolation, cache and encryption boundaries.

title: Workload-token claim under-binding
invariant: Token exchange must bind issuer, audience, subject, workload identity, source context, and lifetime to one intended workload.
attackerControl: Federated token claims, repository or branch identity, namespace, service identity, audience, subject, and exchange request context obtainable by the attacker.
differential: Verification accepts a broad issuer, audience, subject, or source pattern that includes attacker-controlled workloads outside the intended trust set.
requiredProof: Show the attacker can obtain a correctly signed token whose verified claims satisfy the deployed exchange conditions and yield usable broader credentials.
decisiveRejection: Verified claims and provider-side conditions bind one intended workload and the attacker cannot obtain a matching token.
overlaps: CLX-01, signed-capability under-binding, federation, CI/CD identity.

title: Ambient metadata or credential inheritance
invariant: A workload must access only credentials and metadata explicitly delegated to its isolation and authority boundary.
attackerControl: Workload code, network destinations, filesystem paths, projected token locations, host-agent interfaces, and neighboring identity endpoints reachable from the workload.
differential: Workload isolation appears least-privileged while ambient node, instance, host-agent, projected, or neighboring credentials remain reachable and more powerful.
requiredProof: Establish network or filesystem reachability, obtain the exact credential in a safe test or source-equivalent proof, and show its usable scope exceeds the workload contract.
decisiveRejection: Network and filesystem isolation, audience and hop binding, and least-privilege credential policy jointly prevent retrieval or useful operation.
overlaps: SSRF, credential disclosure, container isolation, delegated identity.

title: Workload-to-host boundary collapse
invariant: An untrusted workload must not inherit host, control-plane, device, namespace, or kernel capabilities outside its declared sandbox.
attackerControl: Workload specification, image behavior, mounted paths, sockets, namespace selection, devices, capabilities, and privileged execution flags available at the starting privilege.
differential: The workload boundary is declared as isolated, but host mounts, control sockets, shared namespaces, devices, or capabilities expose a stronger plane.
requiredProof: Establish the intended untrusted-workload boundary and demonstrate one concrete host, control-plane, or cross-tenant operation reachable through the exposed capability.
decisiveRejection: The configuration is administrator-intended authority, or isolation removes the capability and no protected operation is reachable from the workload.
overlaps: Sandbox escape, command execution, CLX-05/12, host filesystem and control-socket access.

title: Unbound serverless or event source
invariant: Event-driven execution must bind the event to the exact authorized source, administrative domain, resource, payload schema, and intended action.
attackerControl: Queue, topic, object, scheduler, web request, or cross-domain event data and source identity available to the attacker.
differential: An event can invoke a stronger function or worker because resource policy or runtime checks omit exact source or payload binding.
requiredProof: Show the attacker can produce an accepted event and trace the resulting execution identity and protected side effect.
decisiveRejection: Resource policy and runtime validation jointly bind source, domain, resource, payload, and action before execution.
overlaps: ACX-12, AIX-08, event injection, confused deputy, queue processing.

title: Secret leakage through deployment artifacts
invariant: Deployment source, plans, state, outputs, logs, layers, environment, user data, and caches must not expose secrets to weaker readers.
attackerControl: A realistically obtainable lower-privilege read path to an artifact or output, and inputs that may cause secret material to be persisted there.
differential: Runtime secret access is restricted, but a deployment or build artifact stores the plaintext or decryptable value under broader read authority.
requiredProof: Identify the exact secret-bearing representation, its persistence and redaction state, the weaker reader, and whether the recovered value is usable.
decisiveRejection: The artifact is reliably redacted or encrypted and decryption authority is no broader than the intended secret access.
overlaps: Sensitive-data exposure, build provenance, logs and backups, credential leakage.

title: Network-policy composition drift
invariant: Effective ingress and egress across every address family, proxy, mesh, load balancer, firewall, and workload policy must match the intended exposure.
attackerControl: Source address or identity, destination, port, protocol, address family, route, and any lower-privilege configuration field affecting composition.
differential: One policy appears restrictive while another layer, address family, generated rule, or proxy path exposes the protected service.
requiredProof: Resolve the deployed composition and demonstrate a realistic lower-boundary path to the exact protected service and operation.
decisiveRejection: The apparent exposure is an isolated source snippet, an administrator-intended choice, or another effective layer blocks the reachable path.
overlaps: Access control, SSRF, service exposure, dual-stack and proxy routing.

title: Encryption-authority mismatch
invariant: Cryptographic key policy and data authority must jointly restrict decrypt, sign, unwrap, and related operations to intended principals and resources.
attackerControl: Principal, ciphertext or data access, key identifier or alias, grant context, service delegation, and rotation or cross-domain parameters available to the attacker.
differential: A weaker principal receives an effective key operation through policy, grants, aliases, or delegation even though protected data access assumes stronger authority.
requiredProof: Compute the effective key action and show the attacker also has the data, ciphertext, or signing context needed for a concrete protected effect.
decisiveRejection: The operation requires both key authority and data access and at least one remains unavailable under every effective policy path.
overlaps: CLX-02/03/12, cryptographic authorization, delegated services, secret access.

title: Mutable deployment provenance
invariant: Reviewed and approved source, module, image, chart, provider, and runtime artifact identity must remain immutable through deployment.
attackerControl: A mutable tag or version, alternate registry or source, module resolution, admission input, update channel, or artifact publish permission.
differential: Review or scanning covers one artifact while deployment resolution selects another attacker-supplied or later-mutated artifact.
requiredProof: Trace resolver precedence and deployment selection to an attacker-controllable artifact that is trusted, loaded, or executed.
decisiveRejection: Immutable digest binding, trusted-source policy, provenance verification, and admission/runtime checks cover the selected artifact.
overlaps: XD-15/16, supply-chain security, dependency confusion, build/runtime identity.

title: Control-plane confused deputy
invariant: A stronger managed control-plane service must bind caller, source, destination, resource ownership, role, and action before acting for a weaker principal.
attackerControl: Caller-selected resource, destination, administrative domain, role, identity, operation, or configuration passed to the managed service.
differential: The caller is allowed to invoke the service, but unbound parameters direct the service's stronger authority to a forbidden resource or domain.
requiredProof: Identify the service execution identity, caller authority, attacker-controlled tuple, and exact forbidden operation performed with the authority delta.
decisiveRejection: Service-side conditions bind caller, source, destination, ownership, role, and action to the authorized tuple.
overlaps: XD-05/20, ACX-05, SSRF, delegated identity, event-driven execution.

title: Option and argument injection
invariant: Untrusted argument values must not select unintended options, response files, configuration, repositories, subcommands, output targets, or other privileged behavior in an invoked program.
attackerControl: Any value, ordering, multiplicity, delimiter, or file reference placed into a process argument vector or tool-specific command object.
differential: The launcher treats each value as inert because no shell parses it, while the invoked program reparses the value as its own option or control grammar.
requiredProof: Derive the exact argument vector, executable and version, identify the accepted target-program grammar, and demonstrate a concrete operation outside the attacker's intended authority.
decisiveRejection: A closed server-owned mapping fixes every control-bearing argument, or the exact program and position provably terminate option parsing without another indirect control channel.
overlaps: CIX-04, PTX-10, QIX-02.

title: Environment-to-execution injection
invariant: Attacker-influenced environment state must not change executable lookup, module loading, interpreter startup, runtime options, or privileged child behavior.
attackerControl: Environment keys or values, working directory, search path, locale, home/config location, loader settings, startup files, or inherited process state.
differential: Code validates the executable and arguments, but process creation or runtime startup consumes unvalidated ambient state with additional execution semantics.
requiredProof: Establish how the attacker changes the exact inherited state and show the maintained child runtime resolves it into attacker-selected code or a forbidden capability.
decisiveRejection: The child uses a minimal server-owned environment, fixed executable resolution and working directory, and no attacker-writable startup or loader source is consulted.
overlaps: CIX-04, CIX-07, CIX-09.

title: Untrusted build and repository hook execution
invariant: Repository or package content from a less-trusted principal must not execute in a runner whose credentials, network, filesystem, or control-plane authority exceed that principal's grant.
attackerControl: Build manifests, dependency metadata, lifecycle hooks, generators, test configuration, workflow definitions, plugins, submodules, or other repository-controlled tool inputs.
differential: Admission treats the input as source or data, while checkout, dependency resolution, build, test, packaging, or preview implicitly executes project-defined behavior.
requiredProof: Trace the attacker-authorized content change to the exact runner phase and show a reachable runner capability that crosses the contributor's intended boundary.
decisiveRejection: Untrusted phases cannot execute project code, or they run with an explicitly intended disposable identity that has no protected credential, tenant, host, network, or publishing authority.
overlaps: CIX-08, CIX-09, supply-chain and CI trust boundaries.

title: Executable configuration injection
invariant: Writable configuration must not silently become code, command, loader, template, handler, startup, or plugin selection under a more privileged consumer.
attackerControl: Configuration field, persisted setting, manifest, rule, handler name, template reference, command fragment, startup option, or config-file location.
differential: The write path validates storage shape or administrative meaning, while a later consumer interprets the same value as executable configuration with broader authority.
requiredProof: Trace creation and consumption, identify the exact config grammar and execution identity, and demonstrate the protected capability obtained at consumption time.
decisiveRejection: The setting maps through a closed non-executable schema to fixed behavior, or its consumer runs with no authority beyond the writer's documented grant.
overlaps: CIX-02, CIX-07, CIX-09.

title: AI-mediated tool execution
invariant: Model output and user-influenced context must not authorize tools or determine high-impact execution parameters beyond the initiating principal's explicit grant.
attackerControl: Prompt, retrieved content, tool description, memory, model-produced argument, approval state, or data returned by another tool.
differential: Orchestration treats a syntactically valid model tool call as trusted intent, while the tool reaches process, interpreter, package, filesystem, network, or automation capabilities.
requiredProof: Trace the controllable context through model/tool selection to the exact executed operation and show missing authorization or scope binding at the authoritative tool boundary.
decisiveRejection: Tool choice and parameters are constrained by a server-owned schema and current principal authorization, with meaningful confirmation for delegated high-impact effects.
overlaps: CIX-01, CIX-08, CIX-09, AI agent trust-boundary patterns.

title: Content classification and handler execution drift
invariant: Untrusted content accepted as inert data must not be routed by a later classification to an interpreter, executable template, plugin, native delegate, active converter, or other handler with code- or host-execution capability.
attackerControl: Filename, extension, media type, magic bytes, archive metadata, discriminator, polyglot content, or downstream routing hint.
differential: Validation selects a non-executable data class, while a later sniffer, router, converter, plugin registry, or delegate chooses an execution-capable handler for the same bytes or metadata.
requiredProof: Identify both classifications, resolve the maintained handler and its effective identity, and demonstrate actual code, template, plugin, native, process, or host capability beyond the accepted data contract.
decisiveRejection: Content is decoded and safely re-encoded into one inert form, or no handler reachable from any accepted classification exposes execution-capable behavior or authority.
overlaps: PDX-05, CIX-14, UPX-02, XX-08

title: Runtime and plugin dispatch injection
invariant: Untrusted identifiers must not resolve arbitrary modules, classes, constructors, exports, methods, serializers, template engines, handlers, or plugins.
attackerControl: Type tag, class or module name, import path, method name, registry key, plugin identifier, discriminator, export name, or stored dispatch field.
differential: A guard treats the identifier as descriptive data, while reflection, autoloading, a registry fallback, dynamic import, or callable lookup resolves executable behavior.
requiredProof: Resolve the exact identifier under production runtime rules, show invocation or initialization, and prove the selected target has an attacker-useful capability under the consumer's identity.
decisiveRejection: The identifier maps through a closed immutable registry to explicitly permitted implementations and unknown or inherited names fail closed.
overlaps: CIX-04, CIX-09, CIX-13, QIX-02.

title: Sandbox capability escape
invariant: Intentionally executed untrusted code must not obtain host, control-plane, credential, network, filesystem, neighboring-tenant, or persistence capability outside the documented sandbox contract.
attackerControl: Program or expression executed inside the sandbox, including its allowed imports, syscalls, files, network requests, tool calls, or runtime objects.
differential: Admission confines syntax or starts an isolated runtime, while exposed mounts, sockets, credentials, metadata, native bridges, privileged operations, or shared state cross the intended boundary.
requiredProof: Establish attacker-controlled execution first, enumerate the exact effective sandbox identity, and demonstrate a reachable primitive with a concrete out-of-sandbox effect.
decisiveRejection: The observed behavior remains inside the documented disposable capability set and cannot reach a protected host, service, credential, tenant, or durable state.
overlaps: CIX-03, CIX-05, CIX-11, cloud and container isolation patterns.

title: Second-order stored execution
invariant: Persisted attacker-controlled values must remain data when later consumed by workers, administrators, schedulers, exporters, renderers, migrations, or automation.
attackerControl: Stored name, field, template, log value, artifact, job definition, configuration, repository object, or imported record.
differential: Creation validates only storage syntax or the writer's context, while a later privileged path reparses the stored value as executable grammar or dispatch state.
requiredProof: Trace both persistence and the maintained later consumer, identify its identity and evaluator, and demonstrate a protected effect unavailable to the original writer.
decisiveRejection: The later path binds the value as inert data, revalidates it for the final grammar and current authority, or runs with no greater authority than the writer.
overlaps: CIX-04, CIX-07, CIX-17, QIX-05.

title: Expression context capability escalation
invariant: A constrained expression language must expose only the documented operators, data, and pure helpers, without paths to general runtime capability.
attackerControl: Expression text, AST nodes, variable names, property paths, function calls, helper selection, or objects placed into the evaluation context.
differential: Validation accepts the limited expression grammar, while evaluation exposes reflection, constructors, prototypes, imports, native objects, filesystem, network, process, or mutable host callbacks.
requiredProof: Pin the exact engine, version, configuration, context objects, and runtime path, then demonstrate a capability beyond the advertised expression contract.
decisiveRejection: The evaluator uses a closed AST and capability set with no reflective or native escape, and the demonstrated operations are explicitly within the caller's grant.
overlaps: CIX-11, CIX-17, CIX-08.

title: Lexical filtering mistaken for confinement
invariant: Security must be enforced by capability isolation and semantic policy, not by rejecting selected spellings while executing the accepted program in a capable runtime.
attackerControl: User-authored code, expression, template, script, computed property, alias, indirect call, alternate loader, or equivalent runtime primitive.
differential: A client, API, or preprocessor blocks known tokens or syntax, while the production evaluator accepts a semantically equivalent construct that reaches the same prohibited capability.
requiredProof: Show authoritative acceptance, execution in the exact maintained runtime, semantic equivalence of the bypass, and a concrete capability crossing the intended isolation boundary.
decisiveRejection: The difference is only validator parity or syntax acceptance, or execution remains within an explicitly untrusted sandbox with no protected capability exposed.
overlaps: CIX-08, CIX-10, CIX-15.

title: Shell grammar injection
invariant: Untrusted values passed through a command interpreter must remain one intended data argument and must not create substitutions, redirections, pipelines, additional commands, or interpreter options.
attackerControl: Any request, message, file metadata, stored value, or configuration concatenated or interpolated into an interpreter command string or command-language source.
differential: The application validates a business value or quotes for the wrong context, while the selected interpreter performs another expansion or grammar pass.
requiredProof: Derive the final command bytes, exact interpreter and mode, show the resulting parse, and demonstrate a concrete command or privileged side effect selected by the attacker.
decisiveRejection: No interpreter consumes the value, or a context-correct non-string process interface passes fixed arguments that the target program cannot reinterpret as control grammar.
overlaps: CIX-01, CIX-02, PDX-08.

title: Untrusted deserialization execution
invariant: Deserializing untrusted bytes or objects must not instantiate attacker-selected executable types, invoke callbacks, resolve classes, evaluate constructors, or traverse a gadget path.
attackerControl: Serialized payload, type discriminator, object graph, metadata, cache or session value, queue message, imported state, or poisoned persistent object.
differential: A guard checks envelope, format, signature, or expected base type, while the deserializer performs dynamic type resolution or lifecycle callbacks with broader capabilities.
requiredProof: Pin the exact format, library, options, allowed types and runtime class path, then demonstrate a reachable callback or gadget with a protected effect in the affected build.
decisiveRejection: The parser constructs only closed data types without executable callbacks, or integrity and provenance prevent the attacker from supplying or replacing the consumed object.
overlaps: CIX-07, CIX-09, PDX-05.

title: Active content processor execution
invariant: Processing untrusted documents, images, media, markup, archives, or generated output must not expose interpreters, delegates, plugins, scripts, local files, or network capabilities beyond the feature contract.
attackerControl: File bytes, embedded metadata, active elements, nested formats, directives, references, processor options, or content that selects a decoder or delegate.
differential: Admission verifies a nominal format or extension, while the actual processor interprets embedded active content or delegates to a more capable engine.
requiredProof: Identify the exact maintained processor, version, policy and selected handler, then demonstrate a concrete processor capability or working vulnerable path rather than citing a library name alone.
decisiveRejection: Accepted content is decoded into an inert representation under a restrictive policy, or the processor is isolated from protected files, network, credentials, processes, and tenants.
overlaps: CIX-06, CIX-08, CIX-18, PTX-04.

title: Execution policy denylist drift
invariant: Every attacker-selectable field, operation, type, option, and execution primitive must come from a closed semantic policy whose default is rejection.
attackerControl: Field name, nested key, operation, handler, option, token, alias, new enum value, or configuration property forwarded toward an execution boundary.
differential: A guard removes or rejects known-dangerous selections, while binding, merging, version drift, aliases, or newly added sink features accept an unlisted equivalent.
requiredProof: Show the bypassed value reaches a real evaluator, loader, processor, or command capability and produces a protected effect; omission from a denylist alone is insufficient.
decisiveRejection: A recursive closed schema maps accepted values to fixed capabilities, rejects unknowns at the authoritative boundary, and no later merge or default restores removed fields.
overlaps: CIX-04, CIX-07, CIX-11, PDX-07.

title: Application protocol grammar injection
invariant: Untrusted scalar values must not become commands, directives, fields, or record boundaries in a downstream application protocol.
attackerControl: Key, value, filter, recipient, header, channel, command argument, delimiter, line break, length, or encoded data inserted into a protocol message.
differential: Application code treats the input as one value, while manual concatenation or context-wrong encoding lets the receiving service parse additional protocol grammar.
requiredProof: Derive the final transmitted bytes, identify the actual downstream parser, and demonstrate an unauthorized command, routing change, data operation, or privileged side effect.
decisiveRejection: A typed client serializes the value in the correct protocol context and the receiver observes exactly one inert field with no attacker-selected grammar.
overlaps: PDX-08, QIX-01, request-smuggling and header-integrity patterns.

title: Untrusted template or expression source evaluation
invariant: Attacker-controlled text must not become template, expression, script, query-helper, or general language source under a more privileged runtime.
attackerControl: Template body, inline expression, script text, rendering rule, validation formula, interpolation source, or stored customization compiled or evaluated by the application.
differential: A guard treats the text as presentation or limited configuration, while the chosen engine compiles it with callable helpers, host objects, imports, reflection, or other active semantics.
requiredProof: Identify the exact source text reaching the exact engine and context, show its executed parse or AST, and demonstrate a concrete capability outside the author's grant.
decisiveRejection: The input is supplied only as a data variable, or a closed non-executable AST exposes no capability beyond the documented authoring contract.
overlaps: CIX-09, CIX-10, CIX-11.

title: External resource expansion in structured parsers
invariant: Parsing untrusted structured content must not resolve external entities, schemas, stylesheets, includes, imports, or transformations with unintended file, network, or execution authority.
attackerControl: Document declarations, entity references, schema or stylesheet locations, inclusion directives, catalog identifiers, nested documents, or parser feature selection.
differential: A guard validates document shape or content type, while the configured parser or transformation pipeline performs external resolution under server-side authority.
requiredProof: Pin the exact parser, version, resolver and feature configuration, trace the resolution, and demonstrate a protected read, request, resource effect, or executable transformation.
decisiveRejection: External resolution and dangerous transformation features are disabled for the consumed path, or a closed resolver permits only immutable intended resources with no cross-boundary effect.
overlaps: CIX-14, PDX-01, server-side request forgery and sensitive-data patterns.

title: Post-validation semantic drift
invariant: The exact canonical typed value approved by the guard must be the value consumed by the sink.
attackerControl: Input representations that undergo decoding, normalization, coercion, merging, templating, expansion, or reparsing after validation.
differential: The guard checks an earlier representation while a later transformation changes its security-relevant meaning before the sink.
requiredProof: Trace every ordered transformation and show the final sink receives a forbidden semantic value the guard did not inspect.
decisiveRejection: One stable canonical typed value is validated once and passed unchanged to the sink.
overlaps: PDX-02, path traversal, SSRF, injection, type coercion, canonicalization errors.

title: Multiple-parser interpretation drift
invariant: Every maintained component must derive the same security-relevant structure and boundaries from the same input.
attackerControl: Raw bytes, fields, duplicate values, delimiters, encodings, and malformed or ambiguous syntax reaching multiple parsers.
differential: A gateway, framework, library, worker, or downstream service interprets the same bytes differently from the enforcing component.
requiredProof: Identify both production parsers and configurations, record their distinct outputs, and connect the sink interpretation to a forbidden operation.
decisiveRejection: The input is parsed once into authoritative typed data or ambiguity is rejected before any alternate interpretation is forwarded.
overlaps: PDX-01/03, request desynchronization, cache poisoning, signature and routing drift.

title: Integrity decision omits consumed semantics
invariant: A signature, capability, allowlist, or policy decision must bind the complete canonical tuple later consumed.
attackerControl: Fields, aliases, encodings, references, defaults, or transformations omitted from or reconstructed after the integrity or authorization decision.
differential: Verification covers representation A while the sink consumes a different canonical, enriched, resolved, or merged representation B.
requiredProof: Identify an unbound dimension, show the attacker changes it without invalidating the decision, and trace the changed operation to the sink.
decisiveRejection: Verification reconstructs and binds the complete canonical sink tuple and that immutable verified object is consumed directly.
overlaps: PDX-06, signed capabilities, webhook integrity, approval drift, cache identity.

title: Declared type and runtime dispatch diverge
invariant: Declared, authorized, resolved, and executed type identities must refer to the same implementation and operation.
attackerControl: Type declarations, object identifiers, registry keys, extensions, discriminators, loader inputs, and aliases used for runtime resolution.
differential: Schema or policy checks a declared type while an identifier, registry, discriminator, or loader selects a different implementation.
requiredProof: Resolve the authoritative runtime type and show it differs from the authorized type and reaches a forbidden sink.
decisiveRejection: The authoritative object is resolved first, strict type equality is enforced, and policy is derived from that resolved object.
overlaps: ACX-11, AIX-03, PDX-05, dynamic dispatch, unsafe deserialization.

title: Authorized principal and execution identity diverge
invariant: The final execution identity must be no broader than the authorized actor or an explicit operation-scoped delegation.
attackerControl: Requests, task content, event subscriptions, connector parameters, callbacks, or configuration that directs a stronger service or operating identity.
differential: Code authorizes one actor while a service, task, event, connector, worker, or operating-system identity performs the sink with broader authority.
requiredProof: Identify both identities, quantify the semantic authority delta, and show attacker control over the forbidden sink behavior.
decisiveRejection: Delegation is deliberately narrowed to the exact operation or the sink reauthorizes the original caller and resolved resource.
overlaps: ACX-05/12, AIX-08, CLX-12, confused deputy, background execution.

title: Scope and cardinality drift
invariant: Authorization must cover every final resource, tenant, namespace, version, child, and set member consumed by the sink.
attackerControl: Parent or child identifiers, revisions, namespaces, arrays, empty sets, wildcard or omitted selectors, and fan-out inputs.
differential: The check covers one parent, tenant, item, namespace, or non-empty set while the sink consumes a child, revision, mixed set, empty-as-all set, or wider fan-out.
requiredProof: Compare submitted, authorized, resolved, and effective sets and identify each member crossing the permitted scope.
decisiveRejection: Every final resolved member is intersected with current caller authority and empty, omitted, and wildcard semantics fail safely.
overlaps: ACX-14/15/19, tenant isolation, bulk operations, revision selectors.

title: Equivalent entry-point control drift
invariant: Every entry point reaching an equivalent protected effect must converge on the same authoritative security decision.
attackerControl: Choice among interactive, API, command, RPC, import, bulk, worker, callback, replay, or compatibility paths and their path-specific inputs.
differential: One entry point reaches the same sink or effective state through independently weaker authorization, validation, or field restrictions.
requiredProof: Demonstrate semantic equivalence of the final effect and the weaker independently reachable control path.
decisiveRejection: All paths converge on one authoritative policy over the same resolved operation tuple.
overlaps: ACX-02/17, alternate mutation, import and bulk bypass, replay and worker paths.

title: Output or side effect exceeds route authority
invariant: Authorize response projection and every mutation, execution, or dispatch independently of route names and coarse verbs.
attackerControl: Inputs to a nominal read, test, validation, preview, update, or metadata operation that influence returned fields or hidden effects.
differential: The declared operation appears low impact while the handler returns protected material or triggers a stronger mutation or execution.
requiredProof: Trace actual response fields and side effects to the final identity and resource and compare each with the granted authority.
decisiveRejection: Both the response projection and every side effect are explicitly authorized for the resolved caller and resource.
overlaps: ACX-13/16, read-causes-write, secret projection, diagnostic and test actions.

title: Approval bound to mutable state
invariant: Authorization, approval, integrity, and cached policy decisions must bind the immutable content version executed later.
attackerControl: Content, references, scripts, workflows, policy objects, aliases, or dependency versions mutable after the decision.
differential: A decision approves one semantic state, but the sink later reloads attacker-modifiable content under the old approval or authority.
requiredProof: Show lower authority can change a security-relevant field after the check and the later sink consumes the changed semantics.
decisiveRejection: Version or digest binding, immutable snapshots, or atomic invalidation ensures the approved state is exactly the executed state.
overlaps: ACX-10, AIX-07, TOCTOU, signed artifacts, deferred execution.

title: State-transition path divergence
invariant: Every protected state transition must follow the allowed graph exactly once and in the required order.
attackerControl: Alternate actions, callbacks, retries, imports, replays, concurrency, and inputs selecting transition or error paths.
differential: An alternate path skips, repeats, or reorders a required validation, authorization, payment, approval, or lifecycle transition.
requiredProof: Establish the reachable pre-state, forbidden edge or multiplicity, complete path, and durable protected state produced.
decisiveRejection: Transactional state constraints and effective idempotency enforce the graph and multiplicity at commit.
overlaps: State machines, replay, workflow logic, payment and lifecycle integrity.

title: Non-atomic check and effect
invariant: Shared-state predicates and their dependent mutations must commit atomically against the same version.
attackerControl: Concurrent operations, request ordering, identifiers, state changes, and timing windows available through normal interfaces.
differential: Code checks shared state and later mutates it without a version condition, lock, uniqueness constraint, reservation, or atomic predicate.
requiredProof: Provide a realistic interleaving and show the datastore permits both conflicting operations to commit and violate the invariant.
decisiveRejection: The datastore atomically enforces the predicate with locking, compare-and-swap, uniqueness, reservation, or serializable transaction semantics.
overlaps: Race conditions, double spend, quota and inventory integrity, XD-10/12.

title: Partial-failure value or authority gain
invariant: A multi-step operation must not leave attacker-beneficial durable state when a later required step fails.
attackerControl: Inputs, timing, dependency failures, cancellation, and retry conditions that select partial-commit paths.
differential: An early side effect commits before later validation, authorization, accounting, or compensation, and the failure path preserves it.
requiredProof: Trace commit order and prove attacker-observable durable value or authority survives the reported failure.
decisiveRejection: One transaction rolls back all effects or complete, guaranteed, idempotent compensation removes the benefit before observation.
overlaps: XD-10/11, retry and compensation logic, payment and provisioning workflows.

title: Limit enforced after expensive work
invariant: Reject excessive size, count, depth, duration, and fan-out before the first expensive allocation or shared-resource operation.
attackerControl: Input size, declared and actual lengths, nesting, compression ratios, query shape, recursion, batch size, and fan-out selectors.
differential: A limit exists but runs only after allocation, parsing, decompression, recursion, planning, or downstream fan-out has incurred the cost.
requiredProof: Quantify the first expensive step, attacker cost, shared-resource cost, reachability, and the limit's later placement.
decisiveRejection: Strict pre-cost bounds or isolation contain the operation before meaningful shared-resource consumption.
overlaps: Resource exhaustion, decompression, parser recursion, query complexity, MSX-11.

title: Amplification and lifecycle escape
invariant: Bound cumulative work, retries, cycles, queued items, stored objects, and retention created by one attacker action.
attackerControl: Inputs that select recipients, branches, retries, event cycles, recursive tasks, durable storage, and retention or cleanup behavior.
differential: One bounded-looking input triggers multiplicative work, cyclic events, durable queue or storage growth, or unbounded retention across stages.
requiredProof: Demonstrate a realistic low-authority trigger, amplification factor or lifecycle, and concrete shared resource affected.
decisiveRejection: Work scales only linearly with attacker traffic or hard cumulative budgets and lifecycle cleanup bound the shared effect.
overlaps: AIX-09, queue and notification amplification, event loops, durable resource exhaustion.

title: Resolver selects unauthorized provenance
invariant: Every logical dependency, image, extension, connector, model, or artifact name must resolve only to an authorized immutable provenance.
attackerControl: Registry or source precedence, namespace, logical name, version, tag, update channel, and publishable artifact candidates.
differential: A reviewed declaration can resolve from another source, namespace, or registry that the attacker can populate.
requiredProof: Trace resolver precedence to the selected attacker-supplied object and show trusted loading, execution, or use follows.
decisiveRejection: Trusted-source policy, immutable digest binding, provenance verification, and runtime verification cover the selected object.
overlaps: CLX-11, dependency confusion, plugin and model loading, supply chain.

title: Build, artifact, and runtime identity drift
invariant: Review, signing, scanning, deployment, and runtime loading must refer to the same reproducibly identified artifact.
attackerControl: Build inputs, generators, mutable outputs, artifact replacement, deployment selection, loader paths, and update channels.
differential: Security review covers source or one artifact while deployment loads regenerated, mutable, differently built, or substituted output.
requiredProof: Trace source, builder, build inputs, artifact digest, deployment selection, and runtime loader identity end to end.
decisiveRejection: Reproducible provenance and digest verification bind every stage to one immutable artifact.
overlaps: XD-15, CLX-11, build pipeline integrity, generated code and release provenance.

title: Envelope policy omits payload semantics
invariant: Authorization must derive from the fully resolved nested payload, attachment, batch member, and referenced object that controls the real action.
attackerControl: Message metadata, nested payloads, attachment identifiers, batch items, references, targets, and action parameters.
differential: A guard authorizes request or message metadata while a nested value or referenced object selects a different target or operation at the consumer.
requiredProof: Resolve the complete payload and show an attacker-controlled nested dimension selects an unapproved target or action.
decisiveRejection: The consumer resolves the full payload first and derives policy from every final target, action, and member.
overlaps: AIX-03, ACX-11/15/17, batch and message authorization, indirect object references.

title: Permissive indeterminate-state fallback
invariant: Missing, unknown, unsupported, timed-out, failed, and exceptional security states must deny or safely degrade.
attackerControl: Optional metadata, malformed input, unsupported versions, lookup keys, timeouts, dependency failures, and exceptions reachable from untrusted input.
differential: The normal successful path applies a restrictive result, while an indeterminate or error path selects a broader default or bypass.
requiredProof: Show the attacker can reliably reach the fallback and compare its effective authority or behavior with the successful path.
decisiveRejection: Every indeterminate state fails closed and cannot reach a more permissive sink behavior.
overlaps: Fail-open authorization, parser errors, timeout handling, unsupported-version fallbacks.

title: Cache key omits the security tuple
invariant: Shared cache equivalence must include every identity, tenant, authority, origin, method, resource, and representation dimension that can vary the response.
attackerControl: Requests that prime or retrieve cache entries and values omitted from the key or vary calculation.
differential: The origin response depends on a security dimension absent from the shared key, allowing one context's entry to be reused in another.
requiredProof: Derive the actual key, prime a shared entry in one authority context, and show forbidden reuse in another.
decisiveRejection: No shared cache exists, responses are never stored, or complete keying and vary semantics bind the full security tuple.
overlaps: AIX-04, cache poisoning, cross-tenant disclosure, authority and representation drift.

title: Control-plane content gains data-plane authority
invariant: Lower-authority configuration authors must not control executable or security-relevant semantics later interpreted by a stronger plane.
attackerControl: Rules, templates, workflows, policies, models, scripts, actions, destinations, and references writable at the lower privilege.
differential: Content creation is authorized as configuration, but a stronger worker, service, event, or credential later interprets it as an operation.
requiredProof: Identify the author, trigger, executor, exact stronger identity, executable fields, and forbidden sink effect selected by the content.
decisiveRejection: Content is inert, immutably approved before use, or every execution is bounded by the author's current authority.
overlaps: ACX-05/10/12, AIX-08, CLX-07/12, stored execution, event-driven confused deputy.

title: Nonce or IV uniqueness failure
invariant: Every encryption mode must receive nonces/IVs satisfying its uniqueness or unpredictability requirement under the same key.
attackerControl: Message count, concurrent encryption, reset/rollback, nonce field, tenant, or key-selection context.
differential: Nonce generation appears unique locally but repeats through counters, cloning, snapshots, truncation, concurrency, deterministic defaults, or cross-tenant key reuse.
requiredProof: Establish the exact mode, same effective key, repeated/invalid nonce condition, attacker observability, and the concrete confidentiality or integrity consequence.
decisiveRejection: Keys differ, nonce allocation is atomic and persistent, or the mode's documented requirement is met for the proven usage bound.
overlaps: State races, key lifecycle, token generation.

title: Encryption without required authenticity
invariant: Security-sensitive ciphertext must detect modification and bind necessary context before plaintext is trusted.
attackerControl: Ciphertext, IV/nonce, associated metadata, storage record, transport message, or algorithm/version selector.
differential: The application decrypts unauthenticated or downgrade-selected data and uses it for authorization, identity, routing, or other protected state.
requiredProof: Show attacker modification survives verification and changes protected semantics; do not infer impact solely from a non-AEAD primitive name.
decisiveRejection: An independently verified MAC or AEAD tag covers ciphertext and complete context before any plaintext-dependent action.
overlaps: Parser semantics, signed capabilities, session tokens.

title: Incomplete signature or MAC context
invariant: Integrity must bind every security-relevant field, including purpose, audience, tenant, actor, action, resource, version, and expiry.
attackerControl: Signed object fields, unsigned envelope metadata, destination, method, algorithm metadata, or replay context.
differential: Verification succeeds over one subset/representation while unsigned or reconstructed fields select different semantics at the sink.
requiredProof: Identify exact authenticated bytes and demonstrate a meaningful field can change or be repurposed without invalidating verification.
decisiveRejection: Domain-separated canonical signing covers the complete operation tuple and verified immutable data is used directly.

title: Algorithm, key, issuer, or key-use confusion
invariant: Verifiers must select a trusted key and algorithm from server policy and bind them to the intended issuer, audience, purpose, and key use.
attackerControl: Algorithm, key identifier, certificate chain, issuer, remote key source, token type, or embedded key material.
differential: Attacker metadata influences verification policy or resolves a key from a broader trust domain than the protected operation permits.
requiredProof: Pin library/version/configuration and show attacker-selected metadata causes acceptance under an unauthorized key, algorithm, issuer, or purpose.
decisiveRejection: Policy fixes allowed algorithms/key uses and resolves identifiers only within an authenticated issuer-specific key set.
overlaps: ATX-03, ATX-15, CRX-03, RIX-02.

title: Predictable security randomness
invariant: Tokens, secrets, keys, nonces requiring unpredictability, and challenges must have sufficient entropy from a cryptographically secure source.
attackerControl: Observation count, generation timing, process state, tenant, reset/fork behavior, or partially chosen token material.
differential: A uniqueness-oriented or deterministically seeded generator is used where an attacker must be unable to predict or search the output.
requiredProof: Identify the exact generator and entropy inputs, token purpose and search space, attacker observations/attempts, and a practical protected action enabled by prediction.
decisiveRejection: The value is not secret-bearing, or an OS-backed CSPRNG supplies adequate independent entropy and downstream attempt limits close the claimed attack.
overlaps: Password reset, OAuth state, session fixation, nonce management.

title: Password and secret derivation misuse
invariant: Human-memorable secrets must use a salted, deliberately expensive, versioned derivation suitable for the deployment and upgradeable over time.
attackerControl: Password, tenant/account choice, stored-hash observation after a separate compromise, or algorithm/version migration path.
differential: Fast/general-purpose hashes, shared salts, unsafe truncation, low work factors, or migration fallback materially reduce offline resistance.
requiredProof: Establish stored representation, effective parameters, attacker access prerequisite, and the security consequence for the actual credential population.
decisiveRejection: A current password KDF with unique salts and adequate measured parameters is used, and weaker legacy formats cannot remain or downgrade after successful authentication.
overlaps: Account takeover, credential lifecycle, migration state machines.

title: Verification oracle or distinguishable failure
invariant: Secret-dependent verification must not expose a practical adaptive signal before integrity is established.
attackerControl: Chosen ciphertext/tag/token/signature, repeated queries, network position, or observable error/timing behavior.
differential: Failure type, processing order, comparison behavior, or response timing correlates with secret-dependent progress.
requiredProof: Identify the secret-dependent branch, observable stable signal, feasible query conditions, and a concrete recovery or forgery path.
decisiveRejection: Authenticate-before-decrypt, constant-work verification, uniform externally observable failure, strict attempts, or environmental noise makes the claimed extraction infeasible.
overlaps: Existence oracles, padding/MAC oracles, token verification.

title: Key scope, storage, rotation, and revocation failure
invariant: Keys must be least-scoped, protected at rest/use, versioned, rotatable, and revocable without leaving independently usable descendants.
attackerControl: Tenant/resource selection, key alias/version, destination change, backup/snapshot, derived token, or post-revocation use.
differential: One broadly shared or stale key remains usable across tenants, purposes, destinations, versions, or revocation boundaries.
requiredProof: Trace actual key resolution and custody, demonstrate the scope/lifecycle mismatch, and identify protected data or authority exposed by that mismatch.
decisiveRejection: Per-scope derivation with domain separation, managed custody, complete version binding, and tested revocation/reencryption closes the path.
overlaps: ACX-04/05, ATX-05/08, secret exposure.

title: Peer or certificate verification bypass
invariant: Secure channels must authenticate the intended peer identity, trust chain, name, purpose, and validity state.
attackerControl: Network endpoint, certificate/chain, hostname, trust store selection, verification flag, or fallback transport.
differential: Encryption is enabled but identity verification is disabled, incomplete, inconsistently applied, or bound to a different host/service than the connection.
requiredProof: Establish a realistic attacker network position or endpoint-control path and show the maintained client accepts an unauthorized peer for sensitive data/action.
decisiveRejection: Platform verification correctly checks chain and canonical service identity, or the threat model does not grant the required network/endpoint position.
overlaps: SSRF, update channels, service discovery, mobile transport security.

title: Primitive, mode, and parameter security
invariant: The selected primitive, mode, curve/group, padding, digest, key size, and verification parameters must provide the required security property at the deployment's lifetime and attacker capability.
attackerControl: Algorithm/curve/group selector, public parameter, key size, signature/ciphertext, downgrade input, negotiated suite, or attacker-chosen message/query access.
differential: Code checks that an algorithm or key is syntactically supported while accepting a broken, downgradeable, attacker-supplied, non-validated, or security-inadequate parameter set for authentication, confidentiality, integrity, or key agreement.
requiredProof: Pin the exact implementation and parameters, cite the violated primitive requirement, establish attacker control/observability and realistic work factor, and derive a concrete forgery, recovery, impersonation, or protected-state effect.
decisiveRejection: A maintained cryptographic implementation enforces a security-appropriate closed suite and validates every public parameter, or the alleged weakness does not break the required property within the system's threat model and lifetime.
overlaps: CRX-04/07, protocol downgrade, certificate validation, password derivation, supply-chain implementation risk.

title: Bound cost before upload admission
invariant: Enforce cumulative byte, part, item, nesting, and time limits before buffering, decoding, hashing, scanning, or persisting upload data.
attackerControl: Request body, multipart stream, declared length, chunk sequence, part count, filename metadata, or resumable-upload state.
differential: A route or schema limit runs after a proxy, framework, temporary store, decoder, or scanner has already consumed the expensive representation.
requiredProof: Trace the first accepted byte to the first material CPU, memory, disk, or connection cost and quantify realistic attacker amplification.
decisiveRejection: Streaming limits, bounded readers, aggregate quotas, deadlines, and cleanup reject the upload before shared resources are materially consumed.
overlaps: REX-01/02/07, parser limits, temporary-file lifecycle.

title: Bind validation to the consumed file type
invariant: One authoritative decoded representation must determine validation, processing, storage metadata, and serving behavior.
attackerControl: Filename, extension, media type, magic bytes, polyglot structure, nested content, or format discriminator.
differential: Admission classifies a safe type while sniffing, conversion, extraction, browser handling, or a plugin later selects a more capable parser.
requiredProof: Identify the production classifiers and final consumer, then show the same accepted bytes resolve to different security-relevant semantics.
decisiveRejection: The service fully decodes and safely re-encodes to an inert format, or every possible consumer enforces equivalent restrictions.
overlaps: PDX-01/05, browser XSS, command execution, parser differentials.

title: Constrain the final storage identity
invariant: Server-owned tenant, owner, directory, bucket, object key, and collision policy must determine the final storage target.
attackerControl: Filename, relative path, object key, tenant or folder selector, case/encoding variant, overwrite flag, or preexisting link.
differential: A guard checks raw metadata or a staging path while normalization, extraction, symlink resolution, deduplication, or object-store semantics selects another target.
requiredProof: Resolve the exact final key/path under deployed platform semantics and show a forbidden read, overwrite, alias, or cross-tenant collision.
decisiveRejection: Canonical server-generated keys, tenant-scoped storage policy, no-follow semantics, atomic create-only writes, and final-target authorization preserve confinement.
overlaps: Path traversal, ACX-07/14, cloud object storage, race conditions.

title: Bind quarantine approval to immutable content
invariant: Scanning, review, and approval must cover the exact immutable bytes and metadata later published or processed.
attackerControl: Replaceable staging object, resumable chunk, mutable reference, version selector, metadata update, or post-scan overwrite.
differential: A scan approves an ID/path while lower authority can change the referenced bytes, type, destination, or version before publication.
requiredProof: Trace object identity and digest from scan input through every mutation and demonstrate later use of content not covered by approval.
decisiveRejection: Publication atomically promotes the scanned immutable digest/version and any mutation invalidates approval before use.
overlaps: XD-09/11, TOCTOU, approval binding, object versioning.

title: Serve uploaded content with inert browser semantics
invariant: User-controlled files must not gain trusted-origin script, markup, credential, navigation, or content-sniffing authority.
attackerControl: File bytes, name, declared media type, disposition metadata, download route, public URL, or redirect behavior.
differential: Storage treats bytes as opaque while a same-origin delivery path supplies executable media type, inline disposition, permissive sniffing, or trusted headers.
requiredProof: Establish the deployed response headers, origin, browser context, victim interaction, and a concrete protected browser effect.
decisiveRejection: Isolated untrusted origin, forced download, fixed safe media type, no-sniff policy, and contextual encoding prevent active interpretation.
overlaps: Browser XSS, response splitting, cache boundaries, content-type differentials.

title: Bound container and derivative processing
invariant: Aggregate extracted bytes, entries, dimensions, frames, pages, recursion, and derivative fan-out must remain within one operation budget.
attackerControl: Archive, document, image, media stream, nested container, metadata graph, or processor options.
differential: Compressed size or one dimension is bounded while extraction, transcoding, previewing, indexing, or thumbnail generation expands another dimension without a cumulative limit.
requiredProof: Pin the actual parser/processor configuration and show realistic accepted input causes asymmetric shared-resource work.
decisiveRejection: Streaming aggregate limits, recursion caps, process isolation, deadlines, and bounded derivative counts contain the full pipeline.
overlaps: REX-02/03/05, archive traversal, parser security.

title: Preserve uploader authority through processors
invariant: Deferred scanners, converters, indexers, and enrichers must not grant uploaded content more filesystem, network, secret, or execution authority than the uploader.
attackerControl: File content, embedded reference, processor directive, external resource, template, macro, or parser-selected handler.
differential: Upload authorization covers storage only, while a privileged worker later resolves content-controlled paths, URLs, commands, plugins, or credentials.
requiredProof: Trace content control to the exact worker identity and consequential sink, including sandbox, network, filesystem, and parser controls.
decisiveRejection: Inert parsing, least-privilege sandboxing, denied egress, isolated storage, and sink-specific authorization remove the authority delta.
overlaps: ACX-05/12, SSRF, command execution, queue boundaries.

title: Authorize replacement, deduplication, and references
invariant: Reuse, replacement, linking, and deduplication must preserve owner, tenant, confidentiality, retention, and content-version boundaries.
attackerControl: Content hash, existing-object reference, replacement request, shared blob ID, clone, restore, or deletion action.
differential: A shared blob or logical reference is authorized once while another owner, tenant, version, or lifecycle state becomes the effective reader or mutator.
requiredProof: Map logical references to physical objects and show a lower-authority actor can infer, read, replace, retain, or delete another scope's content.
decisiveRejection: Per-reference authorization, opaque identifiers, tenant-aware deduplication, immutable versions, and reference-counted deletion preserve every boundary.
overlaps: ACX-07/21, existence oracles, cache keys, lifecycle deletion.

title: Integer overflow before allocation or access
invariant: Length arithmetic must remain representable in one authoritative width and signedness before allocation and access.
attackerControl: Lengths, counts, dimensions, alignment inputs, and other operands used in addition, multiplication, or rounding.
differential: Arithmetic wraps or truncates in a narrower or differently signed type, so allocation uses a smaller value than a later copy or access.
requiredProof: Derive reachable operand ranges, conversion order, wrapped result, allocation size, and the larger native access using the exact build data model.
decisiveRejection: Checked arithmetic and identical-width bounds dominate allocation and every use, or attacker-controlled operands cannot reach an overflowing combination.
overlaps: PDX-04, MSX-02/03, buffer overflow, resource exhaustion.

title: Allocation/access length divergence
invariant: Allocation capacity and every subsequent read, write, copy, or iteration bound must derive from the same validated length.
attackerControl: Encoded lengths, element counts, dimensions, protocol sizes, decompressed sizes, and values selected after allocation.
differential: Allocation uses one length while a native access uses another decoded value, unit, element count, or protocol field.
requiredProof: Trace both values, their units and conversions, the actual allocation, and the exact native operation that exceeds it.
decisiveRejection: The values are proven equal in the authoritative unit or the destination abstraction enforces the allocation bound at the final access.
overlaps: MSX-01/06/11, parser differentials, decompression and file processing.

title: Signed-to-unsigned size confusion
invariant: Reject negative and out-of-range values before any signedness conversion used for a size, index, or offset.
attackerControl: Signed numeric fields, sentinel values, arithmetic results, and values crossing language or interface boundaries.
differential: A signed value passes a comparison and later converts into a large unsigned size, index, allocation, or pointer offset.
requiredProof: Pin the authoritative type, comparison semantics, conversion order, reachable negative value, and final protected memory operation.
decisiveRejection: A pre-conversion range check in the authoritative type dominates every conversion and use.
overlaps: PDX-04, MSX-01/02/06, integer and bounds errors.

title: Escaped object lifetime
invariant: No pointer or reference may outlive the storage, owner, container epoch, callback scope, or asynchronous operation that guarantees its validity.
attackerControl: Inputs or actions that influence object destruction, reallocation, callback order, cancellation, asynchronous timing, or reuse contents.
differential: A reference escapes its valid lifetime and is dereferenced after destruction, free, reallocation, or owner-scope exit.
requiredProof: Show one feasible lifetime trace, the stale use, attacker influence over reachability or timing, and the concrete data or control operation performed through it.
decisiveRejection: Ownership, reference counting, borrow enforcement, pinning, or synchronization dominates all escape and use paths.
overlaps: MSX-05/10, race conditions, callback and cancellation state machines.

title: Double release or allocator mismatch
invariant: Each allocation must have one compatible owner and one release transition across success, error, and cancellation paths.
attackerControl: Inputs that select error unwinding, cancellation, aliases, ownership transfer, repeated cleanup, or mixed allocation paths.
differential: Two feasible cleanup paths release the same object, or a release uses an allocator contract different from the allocation contract.
requiredProof: Trace allocation identity, ownership transfers, both releases or allocator mismatch, and one feasible attacker-reachable execution.
decisiveRejection: Cleanup is idempotent, ownership states are mutually exclusive and enforced, or allocation and release contracts are statically matched.
overlaps: MSX-04/10, error handling, cancellation, partial-failure state.

title: Unbounded index or offset
invariant: Validate every final index and offset against the actual object bounds after all arithmetic and representation changes.
attackerControl: Indices, offsets, pointer differences, sentinel placement, nested lengths, dimensions, and values driving traversal.
differential: An early or unrelated bound is checked, but the final native index or pointer offset can address outside the real allocation.
requiredProof: Derive the final index against the exact allocation and show the reachable out-of-bounds read, write, or control-sensitive access.
decisiveRejection: A language/runtime check or dominating final-object bound covers the exact computed index on every path.
overlaps: MSX-01/02/03/11, parser differentials, spatial memory errors.

title: Uninitialized data exposure
invariant: Initialize every byte and field before it influences a security decision or crosses an observable boundary.
attackerControl: Requests, object variants, error paths, lengths, and field combinations that select partial initialization or serialization.
differential: Padding, stack or heap storage, unions, structures, or error buffers are read or serialized before complete initialization.
requiredProof: Identify the exact uninitialized bytes, the path leaving them undefined, and an attacker-observable output or protected decision they influence.
decisiveRejection: Zeroing or definite assignment dominates every read and exit, or undefined bytes cannot reach an observable or protected sink.
overlaps: Information disclosure, cryptographic state, error handling, serialization.

title: Attacker-controlled format grammar
invariant: Attacker-controlled text must remain a data argument and never become a native format or control string.
attackerControl: Text passed to formatting, logging, diagnostic, localization, or variadic native interfaces.
differential: An upstream layer treats the value as inert text while the native callee interprets it as format grammar and argument directives.
requiredProof: Identify the exact call signature and show the callee parses attacker-controlled directives that reach a read, write, disclosure, or control effect.
decisiveRejection: The format string is constant and attacker text is passed only as a value argument with compatible types.
overlaps: PDX-08, information disclosure, arbitrary write, logging and diagnostics.

title: Foreign-interface contract mismatch
invariant: Both sides of a foreign-function or binary interface must agree on layout, length, ownership, encoding, calling convention, and error behavior.
attackerControl: Values crossing the interface, callback selection, buffer lengths, encoded strings, object variants, and error-triggering inputs.
differential: Managed and native declarations interpret the same call or object with different ABI or ownership semantics.
requiredProof: Pin both declarations and runtime ABI, trace the attacker value across the boundary, and show a concrete invalid access, release, or call.
decisiveRejection: Generated bindings and runtime checks enforce one ABI contract and compatible ownership over every reachable variant.
overlaps: PDX-01/04, MSX-02/03/05/13, serialization and callback dispatch.

title: Concurrent lifetime or mutation race
invariant: Shared native state must have a happens-before relation covering its complete access, mutation, resize, reference-count, and release lifetime.
attackerControl: Concurrent requests, callbacks, cancellation, task ordering, shared-object selection, and operations that resize or free state.
differential: Unsynchronized access observes or uses a buffer, map, reference count, or object state while another execution mutates, resizes, or frees it.
requiredProof: Provide a feasible interleaving, identify the missing synchronization edge, and show the resulting invalid native operation.
decisiveRejection: Locking, atomics with sufficient ordering, immutable snapshots, or thread confinement covers the object throughout its lifetime.
overlaps: MSX-04/05, race and state-transition patterns, asynchronous cancellation.

title: Parser cursor or recursion escape
invariant: Parser cursors must advance monotonically within one authoritative remaining-byte slice, and recursion depth must be bounded before descent.
attackerControl: Nested records, lengths, offsets, terminators, recursion structure, and encoded cursor advances.
differential: A parser uses untrusted lengths or depth without overflow-safe remaining-buffer checks, allowing a terminal read outside the slice or uncontrolled recursion.
requiredProof: Trace cursor, remaining bytes, arithmetic, depth, termination, and the exact final read or stack/resource effect.
decisiveRejection: One authoritative slice or cursor abstraction fails closed on overflow, exhaustion, and depth before every advance or recursive call.
overlaps: PDX-04, MSX-01/02/06, parser differentials, resource exhaustion.

title: Unvalidated privileged address domain
invariant: Privileged native interfaces must validate that every pointer, shared-memory offset, mapped region, or device address belongs to the caller's permitted domain.
attackerControl: User pointers, mapped offsets, shared-memory descriptors, device addresses, lengths, and mapping selections.
differential: A privileged interface trusts an address-like value or validates one representation while the final mapping resolves to protected memory.
requiredProof: Show an untrusted caller controls the address and length, trace final mapping semantics, and identify the protected memory operation reached.
decisiveRejection: Copy boundaries, range checks, pinning, mapping ownership, and access-mode checks cover the exact final address range.
overlaps: Access control, MSX-02/06/09, shared-memory and device isolation.

title: Type, tag, and layout confusion
invariant: Runtime type, discriminator, object header, layout, callback signature, and allocator metadata must describe the same concrete object.
attackerControl: Discriminators, union tags, serialized types, casts selected through input, callback identifiers, object headers, and allocator metadata corruption paths.
differential: A checked or declared type differs from the actual object layout or dynamic dispatch identity used by a native access or call.
requiredProof: Pin the ABI and runtime, trace the mismatched type to a concrete invalid memory access or control-flow operation, and establish attacker influence.
decisiveRejection: Authoritative tags, checked casts, sealed dispatch, generated bindings, or memory-safe runtime checks dominate every use.
overlaps: PDX-04/05, MSX-09, unsafe deserialization, dynamic dispatch, control-flow integrity.

title: Authorize exported, IPC, and deep-link entry points
invariant: Every externally invokable component, message, link, and route must authenticate the caller where possible and authorize the final target and action.
attackerControl: Another app, external URL, deep link, share action, IPC message, exported component, caller identity, nested target, or route parameter.
differential: Registration or routing admits a broad envelope while the handler trusts embedded identity, resource, token, destination, or action under the app's authority.
requiredProof: Inspect deployed export/association/permission state, prove external invocation, and trace attacker-controlled fields to a protected local or server sink.
decisiveRejection: The entry is private, restricted to an authenticated caller, cryptographically associated with the intended origin, and the handler authorizes the resolved action and resource.
overlaps: RIX-07, ACX-06/14, callback integrity, confused deputy.

title: Keep untrusted web content outside native authority
invariant: Embedded web content must not invoke privileged native bridges, local files, credentials, or navigation outside its explicitly authorized origin and operation set.
attackerControl: Loaded URL or markup, redirect, subframe, script message, navigation event, bridge method, local resource, or externally supplied content.
differential: A guard approves the initial page or hostname while later navigation, frame content, message origin, or bridge arguments reach broader native functionality.
requiredProof: Show production-reachable attacker content shares a context with the enabled bridge and trace one bridge operation to a concrete protected native or server effect.
decisiveRejection: Only immutable trusted content loads, every navigation and message origin is verified, the bridge is absent or minimal, and native methods independently authorize exact arguments.
overlaps: Browser XSS, SSRF, command execution, RIX-05.

title: Protect local copies and ambient device surfaces
invariant: Sensitive values must remain unavailable to weaker on-device observers across storage, backup, logs, clipboard, screenshots, previews, and shared files.
attackerControl: Another app, backup reader, shared-device user, notification or accessibility observer, diagnostic reader, clipboard consumer, screenshot, or physical holder within scope.
differential: The primary value uses protected storage or UI while a secondary copy, log, backup, shared path, clipboard, task preview, or screenshot exposes it more broadly.
requiredProof: Identify the exact protected value and artifact, realistic observer under the stated device threat model, and usable confidentiality impact without silently assuming full device compromise.
decisiveRejection: Platform-protected storage and sandboxing, backup exclusion, structured redaction, private sharing, clipboard minimization, and screen protection cover every material copy.
overlaps: SDX-02/04, credential exposure, lifecycle retention.

title: Authenticate the intended server on every network path
invariant: Every client, embedded browser, updater, and background channel must validate the intended server identity and fail closed on transport-authentication errors.
attackerControl: Network-positioned peer, proxy configuration, alternate endpoint, certificate chain, hostname, trust override, redirect, or debug/legacy transport path.
differential: The canonical client validates chain and hostname while another client, callback, embedded view, error handler, or configuration accepts a different peer or clear transport.
requiredProof: Establish the shipped network configuration and attacker position, then show the client accepts attacker-controlled authenticated content that changes a protected result.
decisiveRejection: Supported platform trust and hostname validation apply consistently, overrides are absent from shipped paths, and lack of additional pinning is not treated as a defect by itself.
overlaps: SSRF redirects, update provenance, credential interception, alternate entry points.

title: Bind updates and dynamic code to trusted provenance
invariant: Installed code, modules, assets, policy, and executable configuration must come from an authorized publisher, immutable artifact, and freshness-protected channel.
attackerControl: Update metadata, package or module, remote configuration, distribution channel, mirror, mutable URL, rollback target, signature, or publisher lifecycle change.
differential: Base-package installation is trusted while an in-app updater, dynamic loader, asset pipeline, or configuration path resolves different bytes without equivalent identity and rollback checks.
requiredProof: Trace attacker control of the selected artifact or configuration through verification to actual shipped runtime loading or security-relevant interpretation.
decisiveRejection: Platform update controls or equivalent signature, digest, publisher, channel, freshness, rollback, and runtime-load verification bind the exact artifact.
overlaps: SCX-01/02/03/08, dynamic loading, CRX-03.

title: Bind delegated intents and pending capabilities
invariant: A delegated capability must bind exact creator, recipient, target component, action, data, mutability, lifetime, and multiplicity.
