attackerControl: Obtained pending capability, delegated intent, callback token, mutable fields, implicit recipient, replay, fill-in data, or forwarded capability.
differential: The creator authorizes one semantic operation while the eventual sender or resolver can substitute target, arguments, recipient, account, or repeated use.
requiredProof: Show realistic acquisition and control of the capability and trace the altered or replayed semantics to a protected effect under the creator's authority.
decisiveRejection: Explicit immutable one-time capabilities bind all security-relevant fields and the receiver independently authenticates and authorizes the final operation.
overlaps: ACX-09, RIX-03, confused deputy, replay.

title: Enforce security invariants beyond the client
invariant: Server authorization, entitlement, pricing, limits, workflow state, and integrity must not depend solely on client UI, local flags, obfuscation, or app attestation claims.
attackerControl: Modified client, direct protocol caller, local database or preference, hidden UI route, request field, cached entitlement, or reported device state.
differential: The client prevents or computes an action while the authoritative backend accepts client-supplied identity, role, amount, state, or eligibility without reconstructing it.
requiredProof: Trace a controllable client value through the real protocol and show the server commits a state or disclosure forbidden under its intended invariant.
decisiveRejection: The server derives identity and sensitive state from authoritative sources and revalidates the exact operation independent of client behavior.
overlaps: ACX-02/22, mass assignment, transaction logic, request integrity.

title: Partition cached state across accounts and tenants
invariant: Local caches, databases, files, background work, navigation state, and in-memory objects must be scoped and cleared or rekeyed on logout, account switch, tenant change, and revocation.
attackerControl: Previous account data, shared-device login, account or tenant switch, predictable cache key, restored backup, pending job, offline state, or stale session.
differential: Network requests use the current identity while local reads, queued writes, or UI state retain content and authority from another account or tenant.
requiredProof: Trace a realistic identity transition and show stale local state becomes visible or produces an effect under the wrong account.
decisiveRejection: Every artifact and task is namespaced to immutable account/tenant identity, cryptographic keys and caches rotate, and transitions atomically clear or reject stale state.
overlaps: CBX-01/05, QEX-02/06, session revocation, backup restore.

title: Minimize notification and peripheral disclosure
invariant: Notifications, lock-screen previews, widgets, wearable relays, badges, and quick actions must expose and perform only what the unauthenticated observer is allowed.
attackerControl: Nearby observer, notification listener, paired peripheral, shared screen, preview, action input, reply, or device privacy setting.
differential: Protected content or actions require app authentication while the notification surface reveals equivalent data or invokes the action outside that gate.
requiredProof: Establish default and deployed presentation/action behavior, the observer's realistic access, and the exact protected data or durable effect.
decisiveRejection: Privacy-preserving defaults redact content, user policy is honored, sensitive actions require fresh app authentication, and peripheral payloads are minimized.
overlaps: SDX-01/06, ambient UI surfaces, step-up authentication.

title: Bind biometric and device proof to the protected operation
invariant: Biometric, device-integrity, and possession checks must authorize a fresh cryptographic operation or server challenge for the correct account, session, and action.
attackerControl: Replayed proof, stale challenge, fallback path, local success flag, copied token, changed account, enrolled credential change, or unsupported device state.
differential: UI records a Boolean success or device claim while later local or server actions accept it without freshness, hardware-key use, audience, account, or operation binding.
requiredProof: Trace proof creation and verification and show a controllable stale, replayed, fallback, or cross-account state reaches a concrete protected sink.
decisiveRejection: Hardware-protected key use, fresh server challenges, verified audience/account/action binding, policy-aware fallback, and invalidation on credential change preserve the proof.
overlaps: ATX-01/09, CRX-03, step-up authentication, device trust.

title: Guard/consumer parser disagreement
invariant: Every enforcing guard and final consumer must derive the same security-relevant structure from the same input.
attackerControl: Raw request, message, file, protocol frame, header, or stored serialized value.
differential: One component validates with parser or schema A, while a proxy, framework, worker, library, or service consumes parser B's different interpretation.
requiredProof: Identify both maintained production parsers, their actual configuration, the distinct parsed results, and the forbidden sink behavior selected by parser B.
decisiveRejection: One authoritative parse is passed forward as typed data, or ambiguous input is rejected before either interpretation can reach the sink.
overlaps: Request desynchronization, SSRF, path traversal, query injection, file routing, signed messages.

title: Validation before final normalization
invariant: Validate the exact canonical value used by the sink after every decode, expansion, resolution, and normalization step.
attackerControl: Encoded delimiters, Unicode, case, separators, base references, escape sequences, or nested encodings.
differential: A guard approves an earlier representation that later decoding, canonicalization, base resolution, or framework binding changes into a forbidden value.
requiredProof: Trace the ordered transformations and show the final sink representation violates a boundary that the checked representation appeared to preserve.
decisiveRejection: Canonicalization is performed once before validation, is stable for the supported runtime, and the validated canonical object is used directly.

title: Duplicate-field precedence disagreement
invariant: Security-relevant fields must have one unambiguous value across every layer.
attackerControl: Repeated headers, query parameters, form fields, JSON/YAML keys, cookies, multipart parts, or protocol attributes.
differential: A guard selects first, last, joined, or rejected values differently from routing, authentication, signature verification, binding, or business logic.
requiredProof: Demonstrate the duplicate reaches both components and record which effective value each uses for a concrete protected decision.
decisiveRejection: Duplicates are rejected consistently or a single normalized collection/value is passed through all layers.
overlaps: Request integrity, cache keys, query injection, authorization selectors, signature verification.

title: Type, default, and numeric coercion drift
invariant: Type, range, signedness, precision, nullability, and default semantics must remain stable from validation through persistence and execution.
attackerControl: Numbers, booleans, nulls, strings, arrays, union tags, omitted fields, or boundary values.
differential: Schema validation accepts one type/value while language coercion, database conversion, serialization, arithmetic width, or default merging produces another effective value.
requiredProof: Pin every relevant type and conversion and show the coerced value changes authorization, allocation, state, identity, price, quantity, or another protected operation.
decisiveRejection: Strict schemas reject ambiguous forms and checked arithmetic or typed persistence preserves the validated value.
overlaps: State machines, resource exhaustion, mass assignment, payment logic, native memory safety.

title: Non-execution classification and parser-routing drift
invariant: One authoritative classification must select non-execution parsing, validation, storage, policy, and serving semantics for the same content.
attackerControl: Content type, extension, filename, magic bytes, archive member metadata, protocol discriminator, or format tag.
differential: A guard applies the schema, limits, authorization, or storage policy for one data format, while a downstream parser or router interprets another format with different fields, references, limits, or trust semantics.
requiredProof: Resolve the maintained non-executable consumer, show the two classifications produce security-relevant semantic differences, and demonstrate a protected read, write, policy, integrity, or resource effect; use CIX-06 when the distinguishing capability is execution.
decisiveRejection: One classification and typed parse result is passed forward, or every reachable non-executable parser and handler enforces equivalent schema, authority, reference, and resource restrictions.
overlaps: CIX-06, PDX-01, UPX-02, REX-02

title: Canonicalization mismatch in integrity checks
invariant: Signatures, MACs, hashes, deduplication, and authorization must cover the exact semantics later consumed.
attackerControl: Field ordering, whitespace, casing, excluded fields, alternate encodings, aliases, or values reconstructed after verification.
differential: Integrity is checked over representation A, but the application consumes a differently canonicalized, merged, decoded, or enriched representation B.
requiredProof: Show a protected semantic field can differ without invalidating the check and reaches a consequential sink.
decisiveRejection: A deterministic canonical form covers the complete security tuple and the verified immutable object is consumed without reinterpretation.
overlaps: CRX-03, ACX-09, webhook integrity, cache identity, signed URLs.

title: Recursive merge, prototype, or inherited-default injection
invariant: Untrusted object keys must not mutate shared prototypes/defaults or introduce inherited security-relevant properties outside the accepted schema.
attackerControl: Nested object keys, dotted/bracket paths, configuration overlays, deserialized maps, merge sources, or patch documents.
differential: Validation considers submitted own fields, while a recursive merge, path setter, clone, or later lookup changes a prototype/shared default or consumes an inherited value as policy, routing, dispatch, or execution state.
requiredProof: Pin runtime and library semantics, trace the exact key through the merge, identify the affected object population and later lookup, and prove a protected sink effect rather than prototype mutation alone.
decisiveRejection: Dangerous path segments are rejected before mutation, null-prototype/own-property structures are used throughout, the library blocks the path, or the changed property never reaches a security decision or sink.
overlaps: QIX-03, mass assignment, XX-11, dynamic dispatch, configuration and supply-chain boundaries.

title: Structured-field or record-boundary injection
invariant: Untrusted scalar values must remain one inert field when serialized into headers, records, manifests, mail, logs, terminal output, spreadsheets, or application protocols.
attackerControl: Delimiters, line breaks, quoting/escape characters, control sequences, formula prefixes, continuation syntax, or length fields embedded in an output value.
differential: Validation treats input as one string, while manual concatenation or context-wrong escaping lets the downstream consumer parse extra fields, records, directives, formulas, or control operations.
requiredProof: Derive the final emitted bytes, identify the real downstream parser and context, and show a protected routing/cache/action, code execution, credential disclosure, or audit-integrity effect; malformed or visually surprising output alone is insufficient.
decisiveRejection: A typed serializer emits one canonical field, dangerous delimiters are rejected or correctly encoded for the final grammar, or the consumer treats the channel as inert data with no security consequence.
overlaps: Request/response splitting, command and query injection, cache poisoning, CSV/formula injection, log integrity, terminal escape injection.

title: Multi-stage path decoding and normalization
invariant: Path authorization must evaluate the same stable canonical representation that the final sink consumes after every decode, separator conversion, normalization, and native-string boundary.
attackerControl: Encoded separators or parent markers, nested encodings, Unicode forms, escape sequences, null characters, aliases, case, or values decoded independently by multiple layers.
differential: A guard approves an earlier textual form, while a proxy, framework, parser, operating system, native library, or storage adapter transforms it into a different security-relevant path.
requiredProof: Record the ordered transformations and exact runtime behavior, then show the final target escapes the authorized root or selects another protected object.
decisiveRejection: Canonicalization occurs once before policy, is stable on every supported platform, and the validated canonical object is passed directly to the sink without reparsing.
overlaps: PDX-02, PTX-03, PTX-07, PTX-12.

title: Absolute-path base reset
invariant: Joining an untrusted path to a trusted base must never discard, replace, or reinterpret that base through an absolute or rooted form.
attackerControl: Rooted path, drive-qualified path, network share, URI-like path, alternate root marker, or component whose join semantics reset the accumulated base.
differential: Validation reasons about a relative child, while the actual join or resolve operation treats the supplied form as absolute and selects a target outside the base.
requiredProof: Pin the exact path library, operating system and join inputs, derive the result, and demonstrate a protected target reachable through base-reset semantics.
decisiveRejection: The input is parsed and required to be a relative component sequence before joining, and semantic containment is checked on the final result.
overlaps: PTX-03, PTX-10, PTX-12.

title: Platform path namespace confusion
invariant: Path policy must cover every namespace, separator, case, alias, device, stream, share, and trimming rule supported by the deployed platforms.
attackerControl: Mixed separators, drive or share syntax, device or verbatim namespace, alternate data stream, reserved name, short-name alias, trailing dot or space, or case variant.
differential: A platform-neutral or single-platform guard compares one spelling, while the deployed filesystem resolves another spelling or namespace to a protected target.
requiredProof: Reproduce the exact supported platform's parsing and resolution and show the final filesystem object differs from the one authorized by the guard.
decisiveRejection: The application uses platform-aware component parsing and identity checks on the final namespace, or the relevant path form is rejected before reaching the supported platform.
overlaps: PTX-01, PTX-02, PTX-08.

title: Archive links and special-entry escape
invariant: Untrusted archive extraction must not create or follow links, devices, sparse mappings, nested archives, or other special entries outside the extraction contract.
attackerControl: Entry type, symlink or hardlink target, device metadata, sparse offsets, nested archive, ordering, or later entry that traverses an earlier-created alias.
differential: Extraction validates lexical entry names, while link or special-entry semantics redirect creation, overwrite, readback, or later processing to another object.
requiredProof: Identify the exact archive format and library behavior, derive extraction order and target resolution, and demonstrate a concrete operation outside the authorized extraction tree.
decisiveRejection: Special entries are rejected or materialized inertly, and every creation/open is anchored beneath a trusted directory without following attacker-created aliases.
overlaps: PTX-05, PTX-08, PTX-13, CIX-14.

title: Temporary-file race and alias replacement
invariant: A privileged file operation must remain bound to the same authorized object from creation or validation through use and cleanup.
attackerControl: Predictable name, shared or attacker-writable directory, replacement timing, symlink or hardlink, rename, cleanup order, reopen-by-name, or lock-file path.
differential: Code checks or creates one object, then later reopens its name after an attacker can replace the directory entry or alias the target.
requiredProof: Establish attacker write and timing capability, show the non-atomic check/use sequence, and demonstrate the privileged operation reaches a protected replacement target.
decisiveRejection: The operation uses an unguessable exclusively created handle and handle-relative or no-follow operations without reopening attacker-mutable names.
overlaps: PTX-04, PTX-08, state-race and resource-lifecycle patterns.

title: Upload and download filename injection
invariant: An external filename must remain descriptive metadata and must not select a filesystem target or create grammar in another output context.
attackerControl: Multipart filename, original upload name, download name, extension, path components, header characters, archive name, generated export name, or stored attachment metadata.
differential: Admission validates a filename for display or file type, while storage, serving, archiving, header construction, browser handling, or command invocation consumes it under different rules.
requiredProof: Trace the exact filename into the final context and demonstrate a cross-root file operation or another concrete security effect caused by that context's grammar.
decisiveRejection: Storage uses a server-generated identifier, presentation metadata is encoded for each final context, and no attacker filename participates in path or control selection.
overlaps: PTX-01, PTX-02, PTX-12, PDX-08.

title: Signed object-key representation mismatch
invariant: Authorization, signing, storage, and retrieval must bind the same canonical bucket, container, tenant, object key, version, operation, and expiry tuple.
attackerControl: Object key, prefix, bucket or container selector, encoding, path component, version, endpoint style, signed request field, or value reconstructed after signing.
differential: Policy or signature covers one representation, while a gateway, SDK, proxy, redirect, decoder, or storage backend selects a different final object identity.
requiredProof: Record the signed or authorized tuple and the final storage operation, identify the semantic difference, and demonstrate access or mutation outside the granted object scope.
decisiveRejection: One immutable canonical tuple is authorized and consumed end to end; parent markers that remain literal in an opaque key do not establish traversal.
overlaps: PTX-01, PDX-06, capability and cloud-storage authorization patterns.

title: Filesystem link and mount containment escape
invariant: Filesystem containment must bind the final object identity despite symlinks, hardlinks, junctions, bind mounts, overlays, mount changes, or post-check replacement.
attackerControl: Link or mount creation, writable ancestor, extracted alias, shared volume, overlay entry, replacement timing, or path that crosses an existing trusted alias.
differential: A guard checks lexical components or a prior canonical target, while namespace resolution at use time reaches another mount or linked object.
requiredProof: Establish control of the alias or namespace transition and show the exact final object opened or created lies outside the intended root.
decisiveRejection: Operations are anchored to trusted directory handles with link restrictions and stable mount assumptions, or the attacker cannot create or influence any traversed alias.
overlaps: PTX-03, PTX-04, PTX-05, PTX-12.

title: Virtual hierarchy scope escape
invariant: Resolving a path-like name in a database, content tree, object graph, or document hierarchy must authorize the final node and every security-relevant scope dimension.
attackerControl: Virtual path, parent marker, node identifier, slug, folder, breadcrumb, ancestor selector, tenant or project component, alias, or mount point.
differential: Authorization applies to the entry root or textual prefix, while virtual resolution selects a node under another tenant, owner, project, lifecycle, or visibility scope.
requiredProof: Trace the resolver to the final node identity and demonstrate the final node lacks a required scope dimension that the caller cannot ordinarily access.
decisiveRejection: Resolution is relationship-based under a scoped root and authorization is re-evaluated on the final node with the complete scope tuple.
overlaps: ACX-16, PTX-11, object-level authorization patterns.

title: File and path protocol confusion
invariant: A value accepted as a local relative path must not later become a file URI, remote share, archive URI, template include, module path, or another path-capable protocol.
attackerControl: Scheme, authority, share name, URI encoding, archive delimiter, include syntax, module specifier, base URI, or string accepted by both path and URL APIs.
differential: The guard parses or filters a filesystem-like string, while a later loader, renderer, URL resolver, plugin, or operating system interprets a different protocol or authority.
requiredProof: Identify both parsers and their outputs, show the maintained sink chooses the alternate protocol, and demonstrate a protected read, write, load, request, or execution effect.
decisiveRejection: The input is parsed once into an explicit allowed scheme and relative component model, and the same typed value is consumed without fallback to another resolver.
overlaps: PTX-02, CIX-07, server-side request forgery and template-inclusion patterns.

title: Stored identifier to privileged path
invariant: Persisted attacker-controlled identifiers must not become privileged filesystem or object paths outside the writer's authorized root when consumed later.
attackerControl: Stored ID, name, slug, label, key, filename, tenant value, artifact metadata, or imported record later interpolated into a path.
differential: Creation validates uniqueness or storage syntax, while a later worker, administrator, exporter, cleanup task, or migration joins the value into a path under greater authority.
requiredProof: Trace persistence and later consumption, derive the final canonical target including non-existent parent handling, and demonstrate a protected operation outside the original writer's scope.
decisiveRejection: The later consumer uses a server-owned opaque identifier or revalidates the final semantic target against the writer's current authorized root.
overlaps: PTX-09, PTX-12, CIX-09.

title: Direct filesystem containment failure
invariant: Every attacker-influenced path used for file read, write, create, delete, rename, or serve must resolve to an object within the operation's authorized root.
attackerControl: Direct path, filename, directory, relative component, static route remainder, download selector, output location, or path assembled from multiple request fields.
differential: Code rejects obvious text or joins a trusted base, while parent components, rooted forms, aliases, or missing final containment allow the filesystem sink to select another object.
requiredProof: Derive the final target under the exact platform and operation and demonstrate an unauthorized file effect; for writes, validate the nearest existing parent and creation behavior.
decisiveRejection: The final component path is semantically contained beneath a trusted root, the operation is anchored to that root, and authorization covers the selected object and action.
overlaps: PTX-01, PTX-02, PTX-06, PTX-08, PTX-11.

title: Archive entry target containment failure
invariant: Every ordinary archive member must extract beneath the intended root after all format decoding, absolute-path handling, component normalization, and destination creation semantics.
attackerControl: Entry name, parent components, rooted form, drive or share prefix, separator variant, encoding, duplicate entry, ordering, or nested extraction destination.
differential: Extraction trusts or lexically cleans the archive name, while joining, decoding, platform rules, or library extraction semantics produce a target outside the destination.
requiredProof: Pin the exact format, library, platform and entry metadata, derive the final created target, and demonstrate a write or overwrite outside the extraction root.
decisiveRejection: Each decoded member is required to be a relative component sequence and every create is atomically anchored beneath the extraction root; special entries are separately controlled.
overlaps: PTX-01, PTX-02, PTX-04, PTX-12.

title: Value becomes query grammar
invariant: Untrusted values must remain data and must not create tokens, clauses, expressions, or control flow in a query language.
attackerControl: Request, message, file, imported record, profile attribute, tenant value, or stored text inserted into a query.
differential: Validation treats the input as a scalar, while string construction or a raw-query API lets the query engine parse it as grammar.
requiredProof: Identify the actual engine and query construction, derive the final query or AST, and prove an unauthorized read, mutation, authentication change, or other concrete effect.
decisiveRejection: The exact position is a bound value parameter and no later formatting, reparsing, or unsafe adapter expansion changes it into grammar.
overlaps: ACX-16, command/expression injection, second-order injection.

title: Dynamic identifier, operator, or query-shape injection
invariant: Attacker-selected fields, tables, indices, operators, sort keys, functions, and projection shapes must come from a closed semantic allowlist.
attackerControl: Field names, order/group options, index or collection names, function names, aggregation types, comparison operators, or include/expand directives.
differential: A framework safely binds values but directly interpolates structural elements that parameters cannot represent.
requiredProof: Show the selected structural element changes the target, predicate, projection, execution plan, or protected computation beyond the intended set.
decisiveRejection: Input maps through a closed server-owned enumeration to fixed query fragments and unknown values fail closed.
overlaps: Authorization scope, resource exhaustion, dynamic dispatch.

title: Structured query-object operator smuggling
invariant: Data-shaped input must not acquire query-operator semantics through recursive binding or object merging.
attackerControl: Nested JSON, maps, arrays, GraphQL inputs, filter objects, serialized criteria, or form-to-object expansion.
differential: A schema expects scalar values but permissive binding, deep merge, or database adapters accept operator-bearing objects or unexpected nesting.
requiredProof: Trace the structured value into the engine's query representation and show the unexpected operator changes a protected predicate or action.
decisiveRejection: Recursive schemas reject unknown keys/types and the application constructs a typed query AST rather than forwarding input objects.
overlaps: PDX-03/04, mass assignment, prototype pollution, NoSQL injection.

title: Mandatory security-predicate composition failure
invariant: Tenant, owner, visibility, lifecycle, and authorization predicates must remain mandatory regardless of attacker-controlled filters.
attackerControl: Search text, filter fragments, usernames, tenant labels, wildcards, Boolean expressions, or field selectors.
differential: Concatenation, precedence, grouping, aliasing, or Boolean composition lets an optional attacker filter weaken or escape a mandatory security predicate.
requiredProof: Compare the intended and final AST and demonstrate that out-of-scope records become readable or mutable.
decisiveRejection: Security predicates are separate typed AST nodes combined by fixed server-owned logic and remain present in the final executed query.
overlaps: ACX-07/16, direct-ID scope bypass, search-strategy mismatch.

title: Second-order stored query injection
invariant: Stored values must remain data when later used by reports, workers, migrations, exports, administrators, or integrations.
attackerControl: Persisted names, labels, templates, saved filters, report fields, metadata, or imported content.
differential: Creation validates only storage syntax, but a later privileged consumer interpolates the stored value into query grammar.
requiredProof: Trace both persistence and later consumption, identify the later execution identity, and prove the stored value changes the final query semantics.
decisiveRejection: The stored object contains a validated typed AST or the later consumer binds/revalidates every value in its final grammar context.
overlaps: CIX-09, ACX-05, scheduled reports, deferred execution.

title: Query translation or gateway semantic drift
invariant: Policy and scope must survive translation between query languages, gateways, ORMs, search strategies, and downstream services.
attackerControl: Query options, federation inputs, aliases, joins, expansions, raw-mode flags, or alternate strategy selectors.
differential: An upstream layer validates one query model, but translation drops predicates, widens defaults, changes null semantics, or exposes an escape hatch in the downstream language.
requiredProof: Record pre- and post-translation representations and show a security-relevant constraint is lost on the executed path.
decisiveRejection: Translation is closed, preserves the complete scope tuple, and downstream enforcement independently applies the same mandatory constraints.
overlaps: PDX-01/04, ACX-07/19, GraphQL and federation boundaries.

title: Authenticate the producer and complete event
invariant: Consumers must accept events only from intended producers and bind authenticity to the complete immutable envelope and payload semantics.
attackerControl: Publish permission, topic or queue choice, headers, attributes, body, source identifier, account, destination, or delivery metadata.
differential: Broker or signature policy authenticates a channel or partial envelope while attacker-controlled nested fields select the real action or target.
requiredProof: Establish realistic publish capability and show an unauthenticated or unbound field reaches a protected consumer sink.
decisiveRejection: Broker policy and consumer verification bind exact producer, source resource, tenant, audience, type, payload, and destination.
overlaps: RIX-02, XD-17, cloud event sources, webhook integrity.

title: Preserve the initiating principal through execution
invariant: Deferred work must execute under an immutable operation-bound delegation that the initiator was authorized to create; a technically stronger worker credential must be semantically constrained to that delegation.
attackerControl: User-authored job, event content, scheduling request, claimed actor, delegated credential, or omitted security context.
differential: Enqueue authorization covers one principal while a worker uses a service, owner, trigger, or default identity with broader authority.
requiredProof: Record author, trigger, and executor identities and show attacker-controlled behavior reaches a sink across a real authority delta.
decisiveRejection: An integrity-bound, operation-scoped capability reaches the worker and each effect is constrained by its tenant/resource/action/version and documented revocation semantics, or current reauthorization/least-privilege intersection closes the same path.
overlaps: ACX-03/05/12, XD-05, confused deputy, task execution.

title: Reauthorize the resolved tenant, resource, and action
invariant: The final resolved object, tenant, version, fields, and action must be covered by current authorization or an immutable enqueue-time capability whose intended lifetime and revocation semantics permit the effect.
attackerControl: Object ID, tenant, alias, revision, relationship, selector, batch member, or mutable reference carried by an event.
differential: Producer checks a parent or submitted ID while the consumer later resolves a different object/version or operates after ownership and permissions change.
requiredProof: Compare canonical authorization tuples at enqueue and effect time and demonstrate a forbidden final resource or state.
decisiveRejection: The consumer reauthorizes the exact current tuple, or atomically consumes an integrity-bound capability that fixes the complete tuple and remains valid under the product's explicit revocation model.
overlaps: ACX-01/13/14/20, XD-06/09, stale authorization.

title: Bind schema and type to the resolved handler
invariant: Event version, discriminator, schema, parser, and runtime handler must identify one intended operation with fail-closed unknown semantics.
attackerControl: Event name, version, content type, discriminator, optional field, serializer form, registry key, or unknown value.
differential: Validation uses one declared schema while consumer dispatch, defaulting, migration, or registry resolution selects another handler or meaning.
requiredProof: Trace raw event through every parser and resolver and show the accepted representation changes a protected target, action, or field.
decisiveRejection: One strict typed parse selects the handler, unknowns fail closed, and the validated immutable object is consumed directly.
overlaps: PDX-01/04, XD-04/18, unsafe deserialization.

title: Make delivery replay-safe and idempotent
invariant: Duplicate, delayed, concurrent, or replayed delivery must not repeat a non-repeatable effect or repurpose a valid event.
attackerControl: Delivery ID, retry, redelivery, acknowledgment loss, captured event, duplicate publish, idempotency key, or partition race.
differential: Authenticity is verified but uniqueness is scoped incorrectly, recorded after the effect, expires too early, or is not shared across consumers.
requiredProof: Show two accepted deliveries can reach a durable duplicate effect under realistic broker and failure behavior.
decisiveRejection: Atomic scoped deduplication precedes the effect and downstream operations are independently idempotent for the full event semantics.
overlaps: RIX-03, SMX-02, XD-10/11, payment replay.

title: Enforce ordering, freshness, and current state
invariant: Out-of-order or stale events must not restore obsolete authority, overwrite newer state, or execute after revocation or cancellation.
attackerControl: Delayed delivery, partition ordering, timestamp, sequence, stale snapshot, cancellation race, replay, or backfill.
differential: Consumer trusts event order or embedded state while authoritative version, status, ownership, or permission has advanced.
requiredProof: Provide a realistic delivery ordering and show the stale event passes guards and commits a forbidden durable transition.
decisiveRejection: Monotonic versions, compare-and-set transitions, current-state authorization, tombstones, and bounded freshness reject stale effects.
overlaps: SMX-01/05, XD-09/11, lifecycle and revocation.

title: Make failure, acknowledgment, and retry converge
invariant: Partial failure must not repeat completed effects, create retry loops, retain resources indefinitely, or silently discard required security work.
attackerControl: Poison message, deterministic failure, timeout, acknowledgment timing, retry classification, dead-letter routing, or compensation failure.
differential: Side effects and acknowledgment/offset commits occur in different failure domains, or retry counters reset across queues and services.
requiredProof: Trace effect, commit, acknowledgment, retry, dead-letter, and compensation order and show durable gain, loss, or amplified shared work.
decisiveRejection: Transactional outbox/inbox semantics, bounded end-to-end attempts, idempotent compensation, and terminal dead-letter handling guarantee convergence.
overlaps: REX-06, SMX-04/06, XD-12/14, queue exhaustion.

title: Authorize fan-out and every recipient
invariant: Topic, subscription, notification, and event fan-out must expose data and trigger effects only for currently authorized recipients and destinations.
attackerControl: Subscription filter, wildcard, recipient list, routing key, tenant label, destination, event field selection, or relationship change.
differential: Publisher authorization covers the source event while routing or serialization expands to recipients, fields, or tenants outside that scope.
requiredProof: Resolve the effective recipient set and payload for each delivery and show a concrete unauthorized read or effect.
decisiveRejection: Server-owned routing intersects every recipient with current authority and applies recipient-specific field projection before bounded delivery.

title: Cross-site request action parity gap
invariant: Every browser-reachable state change using ambient credentials must require an attacker-unforgeable request signal.
attackerControl: Cross-origin navigation, form, script-readable request where permitted, content type, method, or alternate route.
differential: The canonical interface enforces anti-CSRF or origin policy, while an alternate method, serializer, legacy endpoint, upload, GraphQL path, or method override reaches the same mutation without it.
requiredProof: Establish supported browser behavior, automatic credential attachment, missing request signal, and a concrete sensitive effect.
decisiveRejection: Credentials are not ambient, SameSite and origin/token enforcement covers every reachable mutation, or the browser cannot construct the accepted request.
overlaps: ACX-02, WebSocket actions, account changes.

title: Callback or webhook integrity under-binding
invariant: External callbacks must authenticate the sender and bind method, destination, audience, exact body semantics, and relevant metadata.
attackerControl: Callback body, headers, path, query, delivery identifier, or endpoint selection.
differential: Signature verification covers only a subset, uses reconstructed data, accepts ambiguous encodings, or is performed before a later semantic transformation.
requiredProof: Identify the exact verified bytes/fields and show an unsigned or differently interpreted security-relevant value reaches the sink.
decisiveRejection: Verification covers immutable canonical request data and audience, and the verified object is consumed without reparsing or enrichment from attacker input.

title: Replay and freshness under-binding
invariant: A valid request or callback must be usable only within its intended time, audience, operation, and multiplicity.
attackerControl: Replayed signed request, timestamp, nonce, delivery ID, idempotency key, or destination.
differential: Authentication verifies integrity but omits freshness, one-time consumption, audience, operation, or payload binding.
requiredProof: Show captured or attacker-obtainable valid material can produce an additional or repurposed durable effect.
decisiveRejection: Atomic nonce/delivery consumption, bounded clock validation, complete audience/action binding, and scoped idempotency prevent reuse.
overlaps: SMX-02, ATX-05, signed capabilities.

title: Trusted-proxy and forwarding-header confusion
invariant: Client identity, scheme, host, and original destination must come only from an authenticated network hop or trusted runtime metadata.
attackerControl: Forwarded client, host, scheme, port, prefix, or original-URL headers reaching the application directly or through an untrusted hop.
differential: Middleware trusts forwarding metadata without proving the immediate peer, or different layers select different header instances/order.
requiredProof: Establish deployment topology and header preservation, then show spoofed metadata changes authentication, rate policy, link/token construction, routing, or a protected decision.
decisiveRejection: The edge strips attacker copies, reconstructs canonical values, and the application trusts headers only from verified proxy peers.
overlaps: PDX-03, magic links, SSRF, cache keys.

title: Credentialed cross-origin policy composition
invariant: Cross-origin read/write authority must be granted only to a precise intended origin set with compatible credential policy.
attackerControl: Origin, preflight parameters, subdomain ownership, null/file origin context, or redirect chain.
differential: Origin reflection, suffix/substring matching, parser normalization, cached preflight decisions, or endpoint-specific middleware widens the effective allowed set.
requiredProof: Show a realistic attacker-controlled origin receives browser permission to read a protected response or perform a meaningful credentialed action.
decisiveRejection: Exact canonical origin matching, no ambient credentials, non-sensitive responses, and consistent policy at the actual deployed edge prevent impact.
overlaps: PDX-02, account takeover, cache boundaries.

title: Upgraded or persistent channel identity drift
invariant: Authentication, origin, tenant, and action authorization must remain valid throughout WebSocket, streaming, subscription, or long-lived RPC use.
attackerControl: Handshake origin/token, channel selection, later messages, subscription identifiers, reconnect, or connection lifetime.
differential: Only the initial connection is authorized, while later messages select resources/actions, outlive revocation, or reuse identity across tenants.
requiredProof: Trace handshake and action authorization separately and demonstrate a post-connect forbidden action or read.
decisiveRejection: Every sensitive message is authorized against current identity and scope, and revocation closes or invalidates active channels.
overlaps: ACX-06/15, XX-03/09, stale authorization.

title: Method, route, and media-type enforcement drift
invariant: Equivalent request representations and routing paths must enforce identical authentication, integrity, authorization, and validation.
attackerControl: Method override, alternate verb, trailing path form, versioned route, content type, charset, multipart boundary, or transport adapter.
differential: Edge/middleware policy keys on one representation while framework routing normalizes or dispatches another to the same handler/sink.
requiredProof: Map both effective routes through the deployed middleware order and show the weaker representation reaches a protected sink.
decisiveRejection: Canonical routing precedes security enforcement or all aliases share one authoritative policy and schema.
overlaps: PDX-01/02, ACX-02, request desynchronization.

title: Conflicting body-framing precedence
invariant: Every hop must use one unambiguous rule for the request or response body boundary.
attackerControl: Conflicting length, transfer-coding, and body bytes in a message sent through multiple maintained hops.
differential: One hop accepts or prioritizes a content length while another prioritizes a transfer coding or other framing signal.
requiredProof: Show the conflicting message is accepted, forwarded with ambiguity intact, parsed into different boundaries, and crosses a reused downstream connection or policy boundary.
decisiveRejection: The first hop rejects conflicting framing or emits one newly serialized request with a canonical body boundary.
overlaps: PDX-01/03, cache poisoning, access-control bypass, cross-request response disclosure.

title: Duplicate framing-field disagreement
invariant: Every hop must handle duplicate framing and routing fields with the same reject-or-select semantics.
attackerControl: Repeated length, transfer-coding, host, authority, or routing fields and their ordering.
differential: Hops select the first, last, joined, or rejected value differently, producing distinct message boundaries or targets.
requiredProof: Record the exact effective value at both production parsers and the downstream request boundary selected by each.
decisiveRejection: All hops reject duplicates consistently or the first hop reconstructs one canonical single-value message.
overlaps: PDX-03, HDS-01/06, cache-key confusion, virtual-host routing.

title: Transfer-coding normalization disagreement
invariant: Transfer-coding syntax and validity must normalize identically before any hop determines a message boundary.
attackerControl: Coding names, case, whitespace, separators, extensions, unknown tokens, obsolete folding, and malformed syntax.
differential: One parser ignores or accepts a transfer coding that another parser treats as active framing.
requiredProof: Pin both parser versions and configurations and show the same field causes one hop to frame a body while the other does not.
decisiveRejection: Invalid or unsupported coding is rejected before forwarding, or the first hop emits canonical framing consumed identically downstream.
overlaps: PDX-01/02, HDS-01/02, protocol normalization.

title: Protocol-conversion boundary drift
invariant: Protocol conversion must preserve one message boundary and reconstruct only canonical routing and framing fields.
attackerControl: Pseudo-fields, body bytes, authority, path, length metadata, transfer metadata, and hop-by-hop fields at the higher-protocol ingress.
differential: A conversion to an older protocol serializes attacker-influenced fields that a downstream parser interprets differently from the converter.
requiredProof: Trace the deployed conversion, exact serialized output, downstream parse, connection reuse, and resulting protected request or response boundary.
decisiveRejection: The converter generates canonical framing, strips conflicting and hop-by-hop fields, and the origin consumes that single reconstruction.
overlaps: PDX-01/02, HDS-01/06/07, routing and cache boundaries.

title: Bodyless and special-method disagreement
invariant: All hops must agree whether special methods, upgrades, tunnels, and informational responses have a body or terminate a message.
attackerControl: Method, override fields, status context, upgrade or tunnel metadata, body bytes, and bytes following the apparent message.
differential: Hops disagree on whether a body or next message exists after a bodyless method, tunnel, upgrade, or informational response.
requiredProof: Show the connection states diverge and attacker-controlled bytes become a distinct downstream request or response.
decisiveRejection: The connection closes at the transition or every hop reconstructs and consumes the same canonical boundary.
overlaps: PDX-01, HDS-04, response-queue poisoning, connection-state confusion.

title: Authority and routing-identity drift
invariant: Authorization, caching, routing, and final dispatch must use one canonical authority and path identity.
attackerControl: Host, authority, path, absolute-form target, forwarded routing metadata, and encoded or duplicate variants.
differential: An edge control uses one authority or path while downstream normalization or forwarded metadata selects a different virtual host or route.
requiredProof: Demonstrate the exact edge identity, final downstream identity, and protected handler or resource reached by the difference.
decisiveRejection: Canonical authority and path are validated once and reconstructed before policy and downstream dispatch.
overlaps: PDX-02/03, HDS-02/04, access control, cache poisoning, proxy routing.

title: Trailer and hop-by-hop policy drift
invariant: Security-relevant fields must not appear through trailers or connection-nominated metadata outside the authoritative policy parse.
attackerControl: Trailer fields, trailer declarations, connection tokens, nominated hop-by-hop fields, and their encoded values.
differential: A downstream hop honors a field supplied through a trailer or hop-by-hop channel that an upstream control did not inspect.
requiredProof: Show the field survives the real transport and changes authentication, routing, framing, caching, or a protected action.
decisiveRejection: Trailers and nominated hop-by-hop fields are stripped, or authoritative policy runs after canonical reconstruction.
overlaps: PDX-03/08, HDS-03/04, header injection, cache and authorization boundaries.

title: Cross-request impact from parser drift
invariant: A parser disagreement must not let one request alter another request, response, cache entry, or protected policy decision.
attackerControl: Ambiguous message bytes, request timing, connection occupancy, and any cacheable or queued follow-up traffic available to the attacker.
differential: A framing drift leaves bytes in a shared connection or queue that a later hop treats as another message or associates with another user.
requiredProof: Demonstrate realistic connection reuse and a concrete poisoned request, bypassed front-end control, altered shared cache entry, or exposed response.
decisiveRejection: The disagreement causes only an isolated malformed-request failure, or connection isolation and closure prevent any cross-request boundary crossing.
overlaps: HDS-01/04/05, cache poisoning, access-control bypass, response disclosure, resource exhaustion.

title: Limit applied after allocation or buffering
invariant: Enforce byte, item, and structure limits before allocating, buffering, copying, or persisting attacker-controlled input.
attackerControl: Body/frame length, multipart part, file, message, collection, string, or declared size.
differential: A size/schema limit exists but runs after a server, framework, parser, or worker has already consumed the expensive representation.
requiredProof: Trace where bytes are accepted and memory/disk is first committed, quantify the pre-limit cost, and identify the shared resource affected.
decisiveRejection: Streaming admission limits, bounded readers, transport limits, or isolated quotas stop input before material cost.
overlaps: Uploads, parsers, queues, native size arithmetic.

title: Expansion, decompression, or recursive structure amplification
invariant: Bound expanded bytes, entries, nesting, recursion, references, and aggregate work rather than only compressed/input size.
attackerControl: Archive, compressed stream, XML/entity graph, serialized object, recursive template, nested document, or chained include.
differential: Admission checks the compact representation while parsing or extraction expands it without aggregate depth/count/ratio limits.
requiredProof: Identify the actual parser settings and a realistic input-to-work amplification that reaches a shared resource.
decisiveRejection: Cumulative expanded-size, entry, recursion, and time budgets are enforced during streaming expansion.
overlaps: PDX-05, archive traversal, file uploads, parser security.

title: Algorithmic complexity and pathological parsing
invariant: Attacker-controlled structure must not select superlinear or unbounded work in validation, matching, parsing, comparison, or normalization.
attackerControl: String shape, regex subject or pattern, nesting, collisions, ordering, ambiguous grammar, or adversarial collection keys.
differential: Length bounds appear reasonable but a chosen structure drives backtracking, repeated reparsing, quadratic copying, collision chains, or deep recursion.
requiredProof: Pin the implementation/engine, derive complexity or measure safely, and show a realistic low-cost input monopolizes a shared execution resource.
decisiveRejection: Linear-time engines/algorithms, strict structural budgets, cancellation, or isolated per-request CPU limits contain the work.
overlaps: Query parsing, sanitizers, canonicalization, native parsers.

title: Unbounded query, sort, aggregation, or result materialization
invariant: User-selectable database/search work and result sets must have bounded cost independent of total deployment size.
attackerControl: Page size, offset, sort/group fields, joins, expansion, aggregation, wildcard, script, time range, or export mode.
differential: The API bounds response bytes but the backend scans, sorts, joins, aggregates, or materializes an unbounded set first.
requiredProof: Establish the final query plan/behavior, caller privilege, data-size relationship, and affected shared datastore or worker pool.
decisiveRejection: Server-owned caps, cost accounting, indexed bounded predicates, query timeouts, and tenant quotas apply before expensive execution.
overlaps: QIX-02/06, exports, multi-tenant scope.

title: Multiplicative fan-out amplification
invariant: One attacker operation must have a bounded aggregate number and cost of downstream calls, tasks, recipients, or resource expansions.
attackerControl: Collection size, wildcard scope, dependency graph, recipients, connectors, targets, relationships, or nested batch.
differential: Individual dimensions are bounded independently but nested loops, recursion, or graph expansion multiplies them beyond the intended budget.
requiredProof: Calculate effective fan-out across every layer and show a low-privilege request consumes a shared constrained resource.
decisiveRejection: A cumulative operation budget, bounded graph traversal, backpressure, and per-tenant concurrency caps constrain total fan-out.
overlaps: ACX-15/20, notifications, workflows, GraphQL, queues.

title: Retry, requeue, and failure amplification
invariant: Failure handling must converge under bounded retries, delay, deduplication, and circuit breaking.
attackerControl: Deterministic failure, timeout, poison message, downstream destination, acknowledgment behavior, or retryable status.
differential: Each failed attempt schedules more work, retains resources, retries without a global budget, or cycles between queues/services.
requiredProof: Trace retry ownership and counters across boundaries and show one attacker-controlled failure produces sustained or growing shared work.
decisiveRejection: End-to-end attempt budgets, exponential delay with caps, dead-letter termination, deduplication, and circuit breakers guarantee convergence.
overlaps: Queue boundaries, SSRF, callbacks, state-machine replay.

title: Persistent storage, cache, log, or temporary-artifact exhaustion
invariant: Attacker-created durable artifacts must have quotas, bounded cardinality/lifetime, and reliable cleanup scoped to the creating tenant.
attackerControl: Object/task/session/cache-key/log-label/temp-file creation, unique names, retention choice, or incomplete workflow state.
differential: Request rate is bounded but each accepted operation creates durable high-cardinality or orphaned state with no aggregate quota or lifecycle reclamation.
requiredProof: Identify persistence and cleanup paths, attacker creation authority, retained cost per operation, and the shared capacity or control-plane degradation.
decisiveRejection: Hard tenant/global quotas, TTLs, cardinality bounds, transactional cleanup, and admission control prevent accumulation.
overlaps: Cache poisoning, uploads, task creation, telemetry cardinality.

title: Tenant quota and shared-pool accounting mismatch
invariant: Every scarce shared resource must be charged to the actor/tenant that can cause its consumption, including delegated and asynchronous work.
attackerControl: Tenant identifier, execution identity, queue owner, delegated credential, target service, or resource-accounting label.
differential: Admission checks one identity's quota while workers, retries, internal clients, or shared caches consume resources outside that accounting scope.
requiredProof: Trace accounting identity from entry to sink and show a low-privilege tenant can exceed its intended share or impair other tenants.
decisiveRejection: End-to-end immutable attribution, fair scheduling, hard per-tenant concurrency/storage budgets, and reserved capacity isolate consumers.
overlaps: ACX-03/04/12, queue identity, delegated execution, multi-tenant caches.

title: Low-cost process termination
invariant: Untrusted input and reachable failure states must not terminate a shared process, worker pool, supervisor tree, control plane, or other availability boundary.
attackerControl: Input value or shape, message or callback order, missing state, assertion condition, exception path, panic, fatal-log branch, abort, exit, or restart-triggering event.
differential: Admission accepts or routes the operation, but an unchecked assumption or unhandled failure crosses the request boundary and invokes runtime or operating-system termination semantics.
requiredProof: Pin the production build and error semantics, trace attacker influence to the terminating operation, identify the shared failure scope and restart behavior, and show practical disruption from low attacker cost.
decisiveRejection: The failure is contained to an isolated request or disposable worker, recovery preserves service within the documented contract, or material disruption requires excluded volumetric traffic.

title: Resource and handle leakage
invariant: Memory, files, sockets, descriptors, transactions, locks, goroutines, threads, tasks, subscriptions, and temporary artifacts must be released on every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, and retry path.
attackerControl: Repeated operation, early disconnect, parse or downstream failure, cancellation timing, retryable response, partial initialization, callback behavior, or branch that skips cleanup.
differential: Admission charges or bounds each operation, while an error or lifecycle path retains a resource after logical completion so repeated low-cost triggers accumulate shared consumption.
requiredProof: Trace acquisition and ownership to the missing release, establish that the resource survives the operation, quantify realistic accumulation and reclamation, and identify the affected shared limit.
decisiveRejection: Structured ownership or guaranteed cleanup dominates every exit, bounded pools and timeouts reclaim the resource, or isolation and quotas prevent cross-request or cross-tenant impact.
overlaps: MSX-04/05/10, REX-06/07/08, state-machine cancellation.

title: Deadlock, livelock, and starvation
invariant: Attacker-reachable concurrency and scheduling choices must preserve bounded progress for shared security- and availability-critical work.
attackerControl: Operation ordering, lock or resource selection, callback re-entry, queue priority, task creation, cancellation, retry timing, dependency cycle, or input that prolongs a critical section.
differential: Individual work is admitted within nominal limits, but lock ordering, wait dependencies, unfair scheduling, repeated conflict, or priority rules prevent completion and retain shared capacity.
requiredProof: Construct a feasible production interleaving or scheduling state, identify resources held while progress stops, establish attacker repeatability and failure scope, and distinguish low-cost asymmetric blocking from load saturation.
decisiveRejection: Enforced lock ordering, bounded waits, cancellation-safe release, cycle detection, fair scheduling, isolation, and recovery guarantee progress without attacker-controlled persistent blockage.

title: Project responses to the caller's field authority
invariant: Every response format and branch must expose only fields, versions, and relationships the current caller may read.
attackerControl: Object ID, field selection, expansion, include, alternate format, error branch, action response, relationship, or batch member.
differential: Object or route access is authorized while serialization, expansion, alternate format, or action output includes fields governed by a narrower read privilege.
requiredProof: Identify the exact protected value, independent denied read path, effective serializer, and attacker-visible response.
decisiveRejection: Field-level projection is derived from current authority and applied consistently to every format, branch, nested object, and batch item.
overlaps: ACX-08/17/21, format divergence, action-response leakage.

title: Keep secrets out of errors and observability channels
invariant: Logs, traces, metrics, audit events, diagnostics, exceptions, and support bundles must not expose protected values to broader observers.
attackerControl: Input echoed in errors, secret-bearing object, header, URL, query, stack context, label, event payload, or induced failure.
differential: Primary output is redacted while an exception path or observability exporter records raw, nested, reconstructed, or high-cardinality sensitive data.
requiredProof: Trace the exact value to the deployed sink and establish a realistic weaker reader through UI, file, backend, tenant boundary, or third party.
decisiveRejection: Structured allowlisting and redaction occur before every sink, access and retention match the data classification, and induced failures reveal no value.
overlaps: Audit integrity, telemetry cardinality, third-party exports, credential exposure.

title: Exclude live secrets from source and build artifacts
invariant: Credentials, private keys, tokens, recovery material, and protected configuration must not be embedded in artifacts readable outside their intended runtime authority.
attackerControl: Repository reader, package or image consumer, client bundle, source map, layer, generated file, build log, test artifact, or dependency cache.
differential: Runtime access is restricted while build, packaging, transpilation, or debugging copies the same usable value into a broader artifact.
requiredProof: Prove the value is genuine and usable or materially sensitive, identify its artifact location, and establish an unintended reader.
decisiveRejection: The value is public/non-secret/test-only or unusable, or secret injection occurs only at runtime and artifact inspection confirms absence.
overlaps: SCX-04/05/06, cloud secrets, browser bundles, hardcoded credentials.

title: Protect secondary copies through their lifecycle
invariant: Caches, exports, backups, snapshots, replicas, temporary files, crash dumps, indexes, and deleted versions must preserve source access and retention policy.
attackerControl: Export request, backup reader, cache consumer, temp-path access, restore, old version, soft deletion, snapshot, or retention choice.
differential: The primary record is protected, redacted, updated, or deleted while a secondary copy remains broader, plaintext, stale, or independently retrievable.
requiredProof: Locate the actual copy and lifecycle path and show a weaker principal can read protected data after the authoritative policy says otherwise.
decisiveRejection: Equivalent encryption/access policy, bounded retention, verified deletion, scoped restore, and redaction apply to every material copy.
overlaps: CBX-04/05, exports, cloud state, lifecycle deletion.

title: Redact the consumed canonical representation
invariant: Redaction must cover the exact structured value and representation sent to the observer after decoding, enrichment, serialization, and formatting.
attackerControl: Nested field, alias, duplicate key, encoded value, alternate serializer, custom object printer, enrichment, or user-selected projection.
differential: A filter masks one name or textual form while another alias, nesting level, decoded value, or serializer emits the original information.
requiredProof: Trace the protected value through transformations and show the deployed redactor misses the final observable representation.
decisiveRejection: Schema-driven allowlisting or typed redaction covers all nested forms before an immutable sanitized object reaches every sink.
overlaps: PDX-01/03, parser differentials, logs, alternate formats.

title: Authorize outbound recipients and destinations
invariant: Notifications, webhooks, analytics, support tools, connectors, and callbacks must receive only data their exact recipient and destination may process.
attackerControl: Recipient, endpoint, channel, template, field selection, event subscription, destination change, or third-party configuration.
differential: Source access or connector-use permission is checked while payload fields, final destination, channel membership, or recipient authority is broader.
requiredProof: Resolve the actual destination and payload, establish who can observe it, and identify concrete data outside that observer's authority.
decisiveRejection: Destination ownership, recipient authorization, immutable binding, field minimization, and egress policy are enforced at delivery time.
overlaps: ACX-04/21, credential persistence, SSRF, QEX-08.

title: Secret plaintext escapes through a secondary channel
invariant: A secret legitimately used inside an authorized workflow must remain non-exportable through responses, previews, errors, logs, caches, exports, generic serialization, ciphertext/key combinations, or downstream results.
attackerControl: The caller triggers a use, test, update, rotate, import, validation, failure, preview, export, or serialization path that handles secret-bearing state without requesting the canonical plaintext-read operation.
differential: The primary secret policy correctly permits internal use without plaintext read, while a secondary copy or observer channel exposes the raw or reconstructable value outside that policy.
requiredProof: Establish that the caller is denied the canonical plaintext-read action, then trace the exact secret representation through the secondary channel to a realistic unauthorized observer.
decisiveRejection: Secrets remain non-exportable handles, every secondary representation is structurally redacted before observation, and ciphertext plus available material cannot reconstruct the secret.

title: Prove metadata and inference oracles cross a boundary
invariant: Status, existence, count, size, ordering, timing, and aggregate outputs must not reveal protected facts beyond the caller's allowed view.
attackerControl: Identifier probe, filter, sort, count, conditional request, error distinction, timing observation, or repeated aggregate query.
differential: Direct content is denied while a secondary signal differs according to protected data or computes over an unfiltered population.
requiredProof: Define the secret fact, observation model, practical query budget/noise, and concrete inference available to the attacker.
decisiveRejection: Uniform responses, scoped aggregation, bounded queries, noise, or insufficient signal makes the protected fact impractical to distinguish.
overlaps: Existence oracles, timing side channels, query injection, aggregate over-fetch.

title: Authorize the deployed proxy and storage context
invariant: Initialization, authorization, delegated execution, implementation selection, and storage layout must preserve the intended owner, role, and state in the actually deployed context.
attackerControl: External caller, initializer, proxy or implementation entry, upgrade selector, delegated call, role input, storage collision, or uninitialized deployment state.
differential: A modifier or initializer appears correct in one code/storage context while proxy execution reads or writes different slots, identity, implementation, or initialization state at the sink.
requiredProof: Resolve deployed proxy and implementation code, initialization history, storage layout, caller identity, and the exact forbidden state mutation.
decisiveRejection: Atomic initialization, compatible reserved storage layout, implementation locking, and authorization evaluated against the authoritative proxy state cover every callable path.
overlaps: ACX-01/14, PDX-04, upgrade governance, storage corruption.

title: Preserve state invariants across callbacks and reentrancy
invariant: External callbacks must not observe or act on partial state, repeat one-time effects, or enter another function that assumes the original operation completed.
attackerControl: Callback-capable token or receiver, external contract, fallback, hook, nested call, alternate function, read-only callback, or reentrant state observation.
differential: One entry has a guard or updates state after interaction while another entry, view, accounting path, or shared resource remains callable against inconsistent state.
requiredProof: Identify an actual attacker-controlled callback edge and a feasible call interleaving that commits a concrete balance, ownership, vote, or lifecycle invariant violation.
decisiveRejection: Checks-effects-interactions, cross-function protection, pull-based effects, and atomic invariant updates prevent every callback from observing or committing forbidden state.
overlaps: XD-10/11, state machines, callback authority, partial failure.

title: Use fresh manipulation-resistant oracle semantics
invariant: Economic decisions must use a correctly normalized, fresh, finalized, and manipulation-resistant value appropriate to the protected time horizon and market.
attackerControl: Oracle update, low-liquidity market state, short-lived capital, stale round, decimal or unit metadata, fallback source, sequencer state, or delayed observation.
differential: The adapter checks that a value exists while omitting freshness, round completeness, source quality, normalization, deviation, or manipulation cost relevant to the sink.
requiredProof: Trace the deployed oracle path and show the attacker can influence or select an accepted value at realistic net cost and extract a concrete on-chain invariant violation.
decisiveRejection: Independent robust sources, suitable averaging, freshness/finality checks, normalization, deviation bounds, pauses, and transaction limits make the claimed manipulation ineffective or uneconomic.
overlaps: PDX-04, economic state machines, arithmetic precision, availability.

title: Bind signatures to domain, action, and one-time state
invariant: Signed authorization must bind chain/domain, verifying contract, signer, caller or recipient where required, action, complete parameters, nonce, deadline, and intended multiplicity.
attackerControl: Legitimate signature, replay, alternate contract or chain, substituted parameters, nonce choice, signer ambiguity, expired authorization, or concurrent submission.
differential: Signature recovery proves an approved signer while one security-relevant domain or operation dimension is omitted, ambiguously encoded, or consumed after the effect.
requiredProof: Show realistic acquisition of a valid signature and a second or altered accepted state transition outside the signer's authorized semantics.
decisiveRejection: Canonical typed domain separation, complete parameter binding, atomic nonce consumption, deadlines, signer rules, and replay tracking cover every execution path.
overlaps: CRX-03, ACX-09, RIX-03, PDX-06.

title: Preserve units, range, and rounding through arithmetic
invariant: Amounts, shares, prices, rates, timestamps, and indices must preserve intended units and bounds with explicit conservative rounding through every operation and conversion.
attackerControl: Boundary amount, decimal or unit choice, conversion order, cast, signedness, precision loss, repeated small operation, timestamp, or extreme state ratio.
differential: Input is range-checked before multiplication, division, casting, scaling, or accumulation produces a different effective value or attacker-favorable rounding at the sink.
requiredProof: Derive the exact deployed arithmetic and show a reachable input/state sequence creates a durable extractable balance or accounting delta, not merely a theoretical precision difference.
decisiveRejection: Checked wide arithmetic, explicit units, bounded intermediates, safe conversion order, and protocol-favorable rounding preserve the invariant across all supported ranges.
overlaps: PDX-04, SMX-03, oracle normalization, accounting drift.

title: Keep internal accounting aligned with custody
invariant: Assets, liabilities, shares, reserves, rewards, fees, debt, and claims must reconcile with actual custody through every entry, exit, transfer, donation, failure, and exceptional asset behavior.
attackerControl: Valid operation sequence, direct asset transfer, fee or rebasing behavior, callback, partial transfer, zero-supply state, liquidation, claim, or rounding accumulation.
differential: One path changes external custody without corresponding internal accounting, or updates internal claims before verifying the actual received or transferred value.
requiredProof: State the accounting equation, trace reachable transitions that break it, and demonstrate durable attacker-controlled extraction, insolvency, or denied rightful withdrawal.
decisiveRejection: Balance-delta accounting, atomic state updates, invariant checks, reconciliation, and explicit rejection or correct handling of exceptional asset behavior preserve equality.
overlaps: SMX-04/06, BCX-05, partial failure, business logic.

title: Make transaction ordering respect a concrete user invariant
invariant: Adversarial transaction ordering must not defeat explicit price, quantity, recipient, uniqueness, fairness, or state-freshness guarantees relied on by a user or protocol.
attackerControl: Pending transaction visibility, priority control, state-changing transaction, competing claim, mutable quote, predictable identifier, or same-block sequencing.
differential: Authorization is valid but execution lacks a user-bound limit, deadline, commitment, batch rule, or state version, allowing ordering to change the protected semantics.
requiredProof: Provide a feasible ordering and name the exact violated invariant and durable on-chain beneficiary; transaction visibility or price movement alone is insufficient.
decisiveRejection: Bound limits and deadlines, commit-reveal or batch semantics, private ordering assumptions actually enforced, version checks, or no extractable invariant delta defeat the claim.
overlaps: XD-09/11, approval binding, oracle manipulation, auction state machines.

title: Constrain upgrades and governance transitions
invariant: Code changes, parameter changes, emergency actions, and governance execution must require the intended proposer, voting power, threshold, delay, scope, and implementation constraints.
attackerControl: Proposal, vote or delegation state, execution target, calldata, implementation, delay parameter, emergency route, quorum snapshot, admin role, or cancellation race.
differential: The nominal governance path enforces threshold or delay while an alternate executor, mutable proposal target, initialization route, role transition, or emergency path reaches the same privileged mutation.
requiredProof: Establish independently obtainable attacker authority and trace a callable path to an implementation or parameter state forbidden by the governance invariant.
decisiveRejection: Unified authorization, immutable proposal semantics, appropriate voting snapshots, threshold control, enforced timelock, cancellation, and post-upgrade validation cover every privileged path.
overlaps: BCX-01, ACX-02/10, stale authorization, state-machine transitions.

title: Bind cross-chain messages to source, finality, and replay state
invariant: A cross-chain effect must correspond once to a finalized message from the intended source chain, sender, contract, domain, payload, sequence, and destination.
attackerControl: Relayed message, proof, source or destination identifier, reorganization, alternate bridge path, replay, sequence, finality claim, or captured valid message.
differential: Verification proves a message or relayer state while omitting source application, destination, finality, domain, payload semantics, or atomic replay consumption.
requiredProof: Trace the deployed verifier and realistic attacker-controlled or replayable message to a duplicate or unauthorized destination state transition.
decisiveRejection: Verified finalized consensus proof, complete source/destination/application binding, canonical payload semantics, and atomic per-domain replay protection cover every route.
overlaps: RIX-03, CRX-03, PDX-06, distributed state machines.

title: Bound gas while preserving essential liveness
invariant: Withdrawal, settlement, finalization, governance, recovery, and other essential progress must remain executable under worst-case adversarially reachable state within chain resource limits.
attackerControl: State cardinality, recipient list, dust entry, failing callback, queue position, unbounded loop, storage growth, adversarial ordering, or cleanup obligation.
differential: Each insertion or item is valid and cheap enough individually while a later all-items operation or single failing recipient blocks mandatory progress.
requiredProof: Show the attacker can create the worst-case state at realistic cost and that the essential operation becomes persistently non-executable with no permissionless bounded alternative.
decisiveRejection: Hard cardinality caps, pagination with monotonic progress, pull-based claims, skip/record failure handling, bounded cleanup, and an effective escape path preserve liveness.
overlaps: REX-05/07, SMX-05, QEX-07, availability invariants.

title: Keep adversarial chain state out of security randomness
invariant: Random selections, prizes, assignments, salts, and secrets must remain unpredictable and bias-resistant until commitment against every participant who can profit from the result.
attackerControl: Block producer/validator choices, timestamp or block fields, transaction ordering, caller-supplied seed, public future value, reveal withholding, retry/revert choice, or oracle request timing.
differential: A value is hashed or labeled random while a caller, participant, block producer, or ordering actor can predict, choose among, withhold, reroll, or abort outcomes before a protected state transition.
requiredProof: Model every actor's information and choices, quantify feasible bias or prediction, and demonstrate a durable economic, allocation, authorization, or secrecy invariant violation after costs.
decisiveRejection: A correctly verified randomness source or commit-reveal/threshold protocol binds participants before entropy is known, handles withholding, separates domains, and consumes each result once without selective retry.
overlaps: CRX-05, BCX-07, SMX-02/05, oracle and transaction-ordering boundaries.

title: Skipped, reordered, or alternate transition
invariant: Every sensitive state must be reachable only through its required predecessor states and proofs.
attackerControl: Endpoint choice, transition order, alternate interface, callback order, status field, or imported state.
differential: The canonical path enforces a predecessor or proof, while an alternate transition directly writes the same final state or trusts client-supplied lifecycle state.
requiredProof: Build the reachable state graph, identify the missing edge condition, and show a durable forbidden state or action.
decisiveRejection: A shared transition service or database constraint enforces the predecessor and proof on every mutation path.
