title: Replay, multiplicity, or idempotency failure
invariant: One authorization, payment, token, callback, or command must produce no more than its intended number of effects.
attackerControl: Repeated requests/messages, idempotency key, token reuse, retry timing, or duplicated delivery.
differential: Validation accepts an already-consumed proof or deduplicates by a key that omits actor, tenant, operation, version, or payload identity.
requiredProof: Show the same authority can be reused and that multiple durable effects survive normal reconciliation.
decisiveRejection: Atomic consumption, properly scoped uniqueness, or idempotent state updates collapse every replay to one effect.
overlaps: ATX-05, request replay, queue delivery, payments, resource exhaustion.

title: Non-atomic check and mutation
invariant: Authorization, balance, quota, uniqueness, inventory, and lifecycle checks must remain true at commit time.
attackerControl: Concurrency, timing, competing updates, shared resource selection, or version value.
differential: A check reads state outside the transaction or lock used by the later mutation, permitting multiple actors to act on the same stale fact.
requiredProof: Identify the isolation/locking behavior and a feasible interleaving that commits a forbidden aggregate result.
decisiveRejection: Serializable transactions, row locks, atomic conditional writes, compare-and-swap, or database constraints prevent the interleaving.
overlaps: Authorization TOCTOU, registration races, double spend, quota bypass.

title: Partial commit and failure-order abuse
invariant: A multi-resource operation must commit atomically or fail without retaining a security-relevant subset.
attackerControl: Batch composition, failure-triggering field, ordering, timeout, cancellation, or downstream response.
differential: Sensitive writes occur before all validation/authorization completes, or failure handling rolls back only part of the operation.
requiredProof: Establish exact write order and transaction boundaries and show an attacker can intentionally preserve a forbidden partial state.
decisiveRejection: Preflight checks cover every item before an atomic commit, or complete compensation is guaranteed and independently enforced.
overlaps: ACX-20, imports, bulk APIs, distributed transactions.

title: Rollback, cancellation, and compensation confusion
invariant: Reversal paths must restore every consumed capability and resource exactly once without granting new authority or value.
attackerControl: Cancel, refund, abort, dispute, timeout, retry, or compensation ordering.
differential: The forward path and reverse path disagree about which actor, amount, object version, side effect, or external action is being reversed.
requiredProof: Trace both paths and demonstrate retained benefit, duplicated restoration, cross-object reversal, or an irreversible side effect.
decisiveRejection: Compensation is bound to an immutable operation record, is idempotent, and reconciles all effects under atomic invariants.
overlaps: Payments, jobs, workflow cancellation, queue retries.

title: Mutable or stale transition proof
invariant: Approval, consent, quotation, policy, signature, and eligibility must bind immutable semantics used by the later transition.
attackerControl: Referenced object, version, price, destination, script, policy, membership, or content after approval/check time.
differential: The guard records only a mutable identifier or stale snapshot, while execution resolves current attacker-modified state.
requiredProof: Show post-check mutation, later resolution, and a material semantic difference executed without reapproval or current authorization.
decisiveRejection: The transition binds a digest/version and complete operation tuple, or every dependent mutation invalidates the proof atomically.
overlaps: ACX-10/13, delegated credentials, signed capabilities, cache invalidation.

title: Client-selected business and economic value
invariant: Price, quantity, currency, discount, fee, entitlement, tax, exchange rate, inventory effect, and derived totals must come from current authoritative server state or an immutable approved quote.
attackerControl: Submitted unit value, quantity, currency, discount or promotion identifier, fee, entitlement tier, line items, derived total, quote identifier, or selection affecting calculation.
differential: Input validation accepts a well-typed business value or verifies only a client-computed total, while settlement, fulfillment, accounting, or entitlement code consumes it without authoritative recomputation or binding.
requiredProof: Trace every value and derivation into the final durable effect, identify the authoritative source that is bypassed, and demonstrate retained value, underpayment, over-credit, unauthorized entitlement, or another protected economic result.
decisiveRejection: The server recomputes from current authorized state or consumes a signed immutable one-time quote bound to actor, tenant, items, quantities, currency, expiry, and final operation.

title: Resolve only from the intended provenance
invariant: Each logical dependency name must resolve only within an authorized registry, namespace, repository, owner, and source-precedence policy.
attackerControl: Public package or image name, alternate registry, namespace, repository fork, mirror, search order, fallback, or ownership change.
differential: Review approves a logical name or internal source while a resolver can select an attacker-controlled object from another provenance.
requiredProof: Reconstruct deployed resolver precedence and show the attacker can publish or control the exact selected candidate.
decisiveRejection: Trusted-source allowlists, authenticated namespace ownership, no fallback, and immutable identity prevent alternate resolution.
overlaps: XD-15, dependency confusion, plugin loading, cloud images.

title: Pin immutable dependency and artifact identity
invariant: Builds and deployments must select immutable versions and digests that match the reviewed and approved dependency graph.
attackerControl: Version range, mutable tag or branch, floating reference, lockfile omission, transitive resolver, mirror rewrite, or republished artifact.
differential: Source review or scanning covers one version while later install, rebuild, or deployment resolves different bytes under the same selector.
requiredProof: Trace declaration, lock/resolution output, fetched digest, and runtime artifact and show an attacker-controllable substitution.
decisiveRejection: Complete lock state and digest verification bind all direct, transitive, platform-specific, and generated inputs.
overlaps: XD-16, update channels, reproducible builds, cloud deployment.

title: Verify provenance with the intended trust policy
invariant: Signature or attestation verification must bind artifact digest, subject, builder, source revision, workflow, environment, and trusted root.
attackerControl: Artifact, signature, attestation, certificate identity, trust root, verification option, transparency record, or missing provenance.
differential: Verification proves that something was signed while policy fails to require the intended signer, builder, repository, workflow, or artifact subject.
requiredProof: Identify exact verifier inputs and policy, then show attacker-obtainable valid evidence authorizes unintended bytes.
decisiveRejection: Fail-closed policy verifies the complete immutable provenance tuple against narrowly trusted identities and current roots.
overlaps: CRX-03, XD-03/16, CI/CD identity, code signing.

title: Constrain build-time and install-time execution
invariant: Dependency metadata, generators, plugins, hooks, and toolchains must not execute attacker-controlled behavior with broader build authority than intended.
attackerControl: Install script, build hook, compiler or linter plugin, generator, macro, task definition, configuration, or tool binary.
differential: Dependency review treats content as data while the build system automatically executes it with workspace, network, secret, signing, or publication access.
requiredProof: Trace attacker control to the exact enabled hook and build identity, including sandbox, egress, filesystem, and secret exposure.
decisiveRejection: Scripts are disabled or allowlisted, builds are hermetic and least-privileged, and no protected credential or output is reachable.
overlaps: Command execution, ACX-05, CI credential exposure, build isolation.

title: Separate untrusted contributions from release authority
invariant: Untrusted code and metadata must not run in a context that can read protected secrets, mutate trusted branches, sign artifacts, or publish releases.
attackerControl: Pull request, fork, contributor-controlled workflow, changed build config, generated path, artifact name, or approval transition.
differential: A CI trigger is treated as low trust while checkout, workflow reuse, later-stage artifacts, or privileged reruns carry attacker content into a stronger job.
requiredProof: Map content author, trigger, runner, credentials, approvals, and publication sinks and prove a real authority increase.
decisiveRejection: Immutable reviewed workflows, isolated runners, read-only tokens, environment approval, artifact verification, and separate release identities preserve the boundary.
overlaps: ACX-10/12, XD-05/09, workflow approval, secret exposure.

title: Bind reviewed source to loaded runtime bytes
invariant: The exact source revision, build inputs, builder, artifact digest, package, image, and runtime-loaded code must form one verifiable chain.
attackerControl: Generated file, omitted build context, mutable base/toolchain, post-build mutation, packaging step, deployment manifest, or runtime loader path.
differential: Review, tests, scanning, or signing covers one representation while build or deployment produces or loads another.
requiredProof: Trace every transformation and identify the unbound stage that can change security-relevant runtime bytes.
decisiveRejection: Hermetic reproducible builds, complete material provenance, digest promotion, admission verification, and runtime measurement bind all stages.
overlaps: XD-16, parser/canonicalization differences, generated code, deployment provenance.

title: Isolate build caches and intermediate artifacts
invariant: Cached dependencies, compiled outputs, workspaces, layers, and intermediate artifacts must be scoped and integrity-bound to trusted inputs and consumers.
attackerControl: Cache key, restore prefix, shared runner, artifact upload, workspace path, build layer, branch, tenant, or partial key match.
differential: A trusted build restores content written under weaker authority or a different input tuple and consumes it without revalidation.
requiredProof: Show attacker write capability, effective cache/artifact key collision, trusted restore, and security-relevant use.
decisiveRejection: Content-addressed immutable caches, complete keys, provenance verification, isolated writers, and clean builds prevent cross-boundary reuse.
overlaps: CBX-01/02, CI poisoning, cross-tenant storage.

title: Secure publisher and update lifecycle
invariant: Publication, delegation, revocation, freshness, rollback, and update selection must preserve an authorized release lineage.
attackerControl: Publisher account or token, maintainer transfer, signing delegation, release channel, rollback target, mirror, stale metadata, or revocation race.
differential: Consumers trust a name/channel or previously valid identity after ownership, authorization, freshness, or revocation state changes.
requiredProof: Establish attacker control of an accepted publisher/update state and trace it to trusted installation or execution.
decisiveRejection: Threshold release controls, short-lived scoped credentials, explicit delegation, freshness/rollback protection, revocation, and verified channels reject the state.
overlaps: Account takeover, CRX-09, stale authorization, update frameworks.
